## abolish/1 and abolish/2 as swipl's (3.36.0)

swipl's abolish/1 takes a predicate away and its declarations with it: a
call of it after raises existence_error, as of one never defined. cocolog's
took the clauses and kept the predicate known -- a dynamic declaration
stayed, so the call failed -- took every clause, a library's too
(`abolish(member/2)` and member/2 failed for good, where swipl's takes
user's import away and lists:member/2 answers again), took an ISO
predicate's clauses and a negative arity in silence, refused a qualified
spec, and had no abolish/2. A minor: abolish/2 is new.

- The C half (lib/builtins-db.cicili, `coco_abolish_pi`): the spec under
  any atom's qualifiers (`coco_abolish_strip`, PL_strip_module()'s), a
  Name/Arity or type_error(predicate_indicator, T); the name an atom, then
  the arity an integer an int holds (representation_error(int), pl-proc.c's
  get_arity()) and not negative (domain_error(not_less_than_zero, A)), each
  unbound an instantiation error, in swipl's order. An ISO predicate is
  permission_error(modify, static_procedure, PI): the 158 of
  `*iso-predicates*`, exactly the ones swipl's abolish refuses (its locked
  system predicates are its `iso` ones, every one asked of swipl 9.0.4).
  A thread_local one is permission_error(modify, thread_local_procedure,
  PI). abolish/2 (`coco_b_abolish2`) asks the same of a name and an arity,
  `abolish(user:p, 1)` among them.
- The clauses go by the reconsult's walk (`coco_pred_forget_where`, two
  modes more: 4 every clause, and 3 the program's alone, for a library's
  predicate, `library` and not `own`), each with a call open on the
  predicate dead where it stands for that call to try still; the backend is
  told once when a clause it holds went -- the walk's rule for every mode
  now, which answers as the old rules did for the three there were.
- The declarations (lib/kb-pred.cicili, `coco_pred_undeclare`): dynamic,
  discontiguous and multifile, public, volatile, transparent, a
  non-terminal, what the tracer hides. The table a fresh store of the
  process reads forgets the name (`coco_dynamic_forget`), and the backend
  hears it as `on_dynamic` with the predicate's DYNAMIC 0, which the
  Zigurat hook answers with `cocolog::forget` (the declaration's row, and
  the clause rows, none by then) -- whether or not this process knew the
  predicate dynamic. The first cut told the backend only of a declaration
  it knew, and a process learns one only on the way to an existence error,
  so one that met the clauses first left the row standing: its own call
  after the abolish failed, its warm finding the row, and the next process
  found the predicate dynamic.
- A predicate a program file took over (msort/2) stays taken, so its call
  raises after, as swipl's user definition is then undefined and the
  system's is not called.

test/files/abolish.pl, new: 88 lines, swipl 9.0.4's byte for byte (3.35.0
differs at 47): an asserted, a declared and a file's predicate abolished,
and what a call, current_predicate/1, predicate_property/2, retract/1,
clause/2, retractall/1, dynamic/1 and assertz/1 find after; public and
multifile reset; a call open on it; the ISO, control, call/N, thread_local,
other system, library and taken predicates; and the arguments of both
arities. test/reconsult.pl's `abolished`: a second process over one
embedded store finds the predicate undefined, declared or not; a fresh
store of the process (run_isolated/2) too; and abolish of member/2 takes
the program's clause out of the knowledge base and leaves the library's.
library/flow: abolish/2's mode (modes.pl) and its write to the knowledge
base (lanes.pl).

Not swipl's (COMPAT.md, the abolish row): `abolish(lists:member/2)` is
member/2 in one namespace, and the library's clauses stay where swipl's
take lists:member/2 away; a program's own between/3, whose clauses joined

user definition hid the system's and a call raises; and a predicate of more
than 1024 arguments is one (swipl refuses it as max_procedure_arity, at
assertz/1 and at abolish/1).

Arms, a build each, the rule taken out (19), each red in abolish.pl or

## A damaged store's message names declare_dynamic again (3.36.1)

3.36.0 taught the Zigurat hook's `on_dynamic` to forget a declaration
abolish/1 withdraws (`cocolog::forget`), and the procedure's name it
chose also went to the failure's message. So a declaration a damaged
store refused said `dynamic: cocolog::declare_dynamic: the store in DIR is
damaged: ...`. Through 3.35.0, as the hook's other failures still say, it
was `dynamic: declare_dynamic: ...`, and test/store-lock.pl's torn-hexmap
section holds that text. CI went red on all three jobs (run 42340567701,
store-lock alone); the 3.36.0 narrow cases had not run store-lock.

`coco_zg_on_dynamic` (lib/zigurat-kb.cicili) keeps the package-qualified
name for the call and gives the failure the short one, `declare_dynamic` or
`forget`. store-lock is red on 3.36.0 and green on 3.36.1.


## listing/1's argument as swipl's (3.37.0)

swipl's listing/1 reads its argument by library(listing)'s listing_/2 and
boot/dwim.pl's '$find_predicate'/2. cocolog's took a name or Name/Arity
alone: it failed when the spec named nothing, and anything else -- a head,
a list, Name//Arity, a qualified spec, an unbound one -- stopped the query
with an error no catch/3 saw (`listing/1 needs a name or Name/Arity`). A
minor: every one of those is new.

- The argument (lib/solve-db.cicili, `coco_listing_spec`,
  `coco_listing_strip`, `coco_listing_one`). The qualifiers come off as
  strip_module/3 takes them, the innermost atom the listing's own module.
  A variable one is every module and ends the strip, so `_:user:yy/2` asks
  for (:)/2. An unbound spec is the module's own predicates. A proper list
  is each element in order, under the list's qualifier, the element's own
  off for its search (and named by its error). `Name//Arity` is
  Name/(Arity+2), evaluated, its errors as name_arity/3's (the `:MAP` row
  `'$dwim':name_arity/3`). A compound is a head: only the clauses whose
  head unifies with it are written, unified and undone (`\+ \+`), a
  single-sided rule's head the one before its guard. Anything else is
  type_error(predicate_indicator, S). A negative arity of an atom name is
  domain_error(not_less_than_zero, A), with context(system:functor/3, _),
  as swipl's search and its library index meet it; of an unbound name
  nothing is found (`_/(-1)`). A spec that finds nothing is
  error(existence_error(procedure, S), context(toplevel, 'DWIM could not
  correct goal')), S with `user:` taken off. swipl's toplevel offers a near
  name on its terminal; cocolog offers none.
- What a spec finds, sorted as Module:Name/Arity (`coco_listing_found`,
  `coco_listing_before`):
  - The store's predicates that a live clause or a dynamic, discontiguous
    or multifile declaration defines, a library's too.
  - The system's, as `%   Foreign: system:atom_length/2`: a C row, or the
    library's clauses where swipl's predicate is C (`coco_listing_sysdef`,
    over lib/swipl-det.cicili's `*swipl-foreign*`: between/3,
    atom_concat/3, nb_current/2).
  - A program's own definition of a system name beside it, under swipl's
    `%   NOTE: system definition has been overruled for msort/2`.

  An unbound name keeps to the qualifier's module, where the spec names one
  (`listing(lsm:_/1)`, `[lsm:_]`). Otherwise it finds the program's
  predicates, as current_predicate/1 walks them; a name given is searched in
  the one namespace.
- THE CANDIDATES ARE READ FIRST (`coco_pred_ensure`): a predicate of the
  knowledge base keeps its clauses in the backend until something calls
  it. The first cut judged by what the process had read, and a second
  process over an embedded store called a consulted predicate unknown.
- A module's own predicates (`coco_listing_module`, swipl's list_module/2):
  - listing/0, `listing(_)` and `listing(user:_)`: user's, which is the
    program's. A module/2 read's file is its module's, which swipl's user
    imports, so through 3.36.0 listing/0 also wrote them.
  - `listing(lsm:_)`: lsm's, a library's too.
  - `listing(_:_)`: the program's predicates of every module. swipl's also
    writes every library it loaded.

  A name that begins with `$` is left out, as swipl's leaves it out without
  access_level system. A blank line goes before each predicate, as
  list_module/2 writes it, where through 3.36.0 listing/0 wrote it after.
  The order is the store's, where swipl's walks its procedure table.
- The writing (`coco_listing_pred`):
  - A predicate's module is written unless it is the listing's:
    `lsm:mp(1).`, and `user:yy(a, b).` where the listing is lsm's, as
    swipl's hide_module/3.
  - None is written under a variable context; the system's Foreign line
    follows the same rule.
  - A declaration is written as write_declarations/2 writes it, `:- ~q.`:
    `:- dynamic 'z q'/1.` and `:- dynamic lsm:md/1.`, where through 3.36.0
    the name went out unquoted, `:- dynamic z q/1.`.
  - A module/2 read's declaration names its predicate's module, as its first
    clause does (`coco_decl_pi` notes `pmod`, lib/kb-pred.cicili).

test/files/listing_spec.pl, new: 478 lines, swipl 9.0.4's byte for byte
(3.36.0 differs at line 3 and stops at line 9). It covers:

- the errors, lists, heads, names and arities;
- the system's predicates, the declarations, a module's predicates;
- the qualifiers, a variable one among them;
- a module's own predicates (lsn, a module of one predicate: the order
  within a module is swipl's table's);
- user's and every module's, held to pieces of their text built at run
  time, so no clause of the case holds them. One piece is cocolog's
  async_workers/1, which swipl has nowhere.

test/files.pl writes the two fixture modules. test/repl.pl holds listing/0's
blank line, and tty_size/2 unknown. test/reconsult.pl's `listed` holds a
second process listing a consulted predicate by name and by Name/Arity, and
the existence error. test/solve.cicili: listing/1 of an unknown predicate
raises. library/flow/modes.pl: listing/1's argument is `?`.

Not swipl's (COMPAT.md, the listing row):

- A module qualifier is no module to a name in the one namespace:
  `listing(lists:zz)` writes user's `user:zz(1).`, where swipl's has none.
- A system predicate swipl defines in Prolog (format/1, dynamic/1, call/1,
  ','/2) is a foreign one.
- A library's clauses are cocolog's own, with no module where its text
  names none.
- tty_size/2, which cocolog does not define, is unknown.
- A near spec is unknown, with no offer and no search: `zz/a` raises
  swipl's type_error(evaluable, a/0).
- An arity past any term is unknown, where swipl's library index runs out

- A partial list is '.'/2's.
- `_/_` and `[user:_]` find the program's alone, where swipl's walks every
  module, the system's too.
- A module's own predicates come in the store's order.

Arms, a build each, the rule taken out (43). Each is red in
listing_spec.pl, test/repl.pl or test/reconsult.pl's `listed`, and the arm

- The argument: the existence error, the type error, a list each element,

## clause/2 of a predicate written in C raises, as swipl's (3.38.0)

swipl's clause/2 refuses to show a predicate written in C: pl-proc.c raises
error(permission_error(access, private_procedure, Name/Arity),
context(system:clause/2, _)). cocolog's failed, as of a predicate with no
clauses, and for the predicates its library writes as clauses where swipl
writes them in C it showed its own (`clause(between(_, _, _), B)` gave
`integer(Z), !, '$between'(X, Y, Z, N)`). A minor: the error is new, and
clause/2's qualifiers are swipl's.

- The rule (lib/solve-db.cicili, `coco_db_private`): clause/2 raises for
  what listing/1 writes as the system's, `%   Foreign:` -- a construct, a C
  row of the engine or of a compiled-in module (a loaded library(stream)'s
  too), and a library's clauses where swipl writes the predicate in C
  (lib/swipl-det.cicili's `*swipl-foreign*`: between/3, atom_concat/3,
  sub_atom/5, string_concat/3, nb_current/2) -- unless the program defines
  the name itself: msort/2 a file took over, a dynamic declaration, and the
  facts library(reasoning) asserts under number/1's name and reads back
  with clause/2, which must go on answering (test/errors.pl's
  `assertz(number(dos))` check).
- The qualifiers (`coco_db_unq_atoms`), as PL_strip_module() takes them:
  an atom's come off, so `M:p(X)` with M unbound, `f(x):p` and `[]:p` (the
  list's end is no atom) stay heads of (:)/2, which has no clause -- through
  3.37.0 any qualifier came off and p/1's clauses answered -- and the
  innermost `system` asks the system's definition alone:
  `system:msort(_, _)` raises though the program defines msort/2, and
  `system:zz(_)` of a program's zz/1 finds nothing.
- The helpers listing/1 asks (`coco_listing_sys`, `coco_listing_sysdef`,
  `coco_listing_found`) moved above the clause/2 walk, which asks them too.

test/files/clause_private.pl, new: 219 lines, swipl 9.0.4's byte for byte
(3.37.0 differs at line 3). It holds:

- 157 predicates swipl writes in C that cocolog defines, every one of them:
  the control, the type tests, the term builtins, arithmetic, text, the
  database, the globals, output and the files' predicates;
- a system name the program defines, unqualified and under `system:` and

- the qualifiers: `system:`, `user:`, `lists:`, a variable, a compound,

- the errors: an unbound head, a number, a float, and each under a

Not swipl's (COMPAT.md):

- What cocolog writes in C where swipl writes it in Prolog -- the control

## repeat/0 as swipl's (3.39.0)

repeat/0 is swipl's ISO builtin, written in C: it answers at every retry and
keeps its choice point for ever, so a cut is what ends it. Through 3.38.0
cocolog had no repeat/0: a call raised existence_error, and a program that
wrote its own got a predicate of its own. A minor: the builtin is new.

- The row (lib/solve.cicili's `*builtins*`, `coco_bi_repeat` in
  lib/solve-text.cicili) answers -2, as arg/3's does with its index
  unbound, and the step hands the goal to `coco_walk`. An atom goal's row
  is called through `coco_builtin`, not `coco_builtin_call`, so the loop's
  atom path asks the -2 as well: a fourth caller beside the step's compound
  path, an environment's BUILTIN unit and the `:` construct's.
- The walk (`coco_walk`): repeat/0's goal has no arguments, and its WALK
  frame's place is bit 49 of `clause_ix`, which no other walk sets and
  which never moves. Its retry (`coco_walk_retry`) answers again, with the
  Redo and the Exit where the printer shows the call, swipl's ports.
- A program file's own clause for repeat/0 is refused at its load, as any
  ISO predicate's is (`repeat :- true.` reads `No permission to modify
  static procedure `repeat/0'`, in both systems).
- clause/2 raises permission_error(access, private_procedure, repeat/0);
  predicate_property/2 answers `built_in`, `foreign`, `static` and
  `defined`; current_predicate/1 answers; listing/1 writes `%   Foreign:
  system:repeat/0`; abolish/1 refuses it -- each as swipl's.

A GUARDED FRAME'S LAST CALL THAT ANSWERS WITH ITS WALK'S FRAME KEPT raises
swipl's foreign error. swipl's I_DEPART hands the guard to the builtin, and
the builtin's exit with a choice point raises
determinism_error(PI, det, nondet, guard_in_caller), context(system:N/A, _).
PI is the builtin's own unless a choice point younger than the call stood
(then the guarded frame's): `p :- $, repeat.` is
determinism_error(repeat/0, ...), and `p :- $, member(_, [1, 2]), repeat.`
is determinism_error(p/0, ..., guard_in_caller) with context
system:repeat/0. `coco_walk` asks `coco_det_bfail`, whose WHAT says
`nondet` (or `fail`, as before, for a builtin that failed). The walk's frame
is dropped first, so that the guard asks of what stood before the call, and
put back if nothing is raised. This holds for arg/3's walk too: through
3.38.0 `p :- $, arg(_, f(a, b), _).` raised the guard's own
determinism_error(p/0, det, nondet, guard), naming the clause.

test/files/repeat.pl, new: 66 lines, swipl 9.0.4's byte for byte (3.38.0
differs at line 1). It holds:
- its answers, counted with nb_setval/2, and the ISO idiom that drains
  the database;
- the control constructs around it: call/1, once/1, \+, if-then-else,
  *->, catch/3, findall/3 and forall/2;
- what a determinism guard makes of it -- `$(repeat)`, a clause's last
  call, one with a younger choice point, one that took the guard through a
  call -- and of arg/3's and char_type/2's walks;
- clause/2, predicate_property/2, current_predicate/1 and listing/1;
- abolish/1, repeat/1 and call/2's errors;
- the program's own clause, refused at the load.

test/trace.pl: three queries over test/trace-program.pl's `rp/1` and `rq/0`,
held to swipl's ports (108 checks). test/engine.pl's `repeat_runs` holds the
case's answers under trace, under a collector every 2000 cells and under a
freeze's materialisation (COCOLOG_KMAT=2), and a machine frozen and thawed
each 25 inferences that answers again at each retry of the frame it thawed,
its count kept by nb_setarg/3. library/flow/modes.pl: repeat/0 is nondet,
and the tables are rebuilt.

Not swipl's (COMPAT.md): predicate_property/2 gives no builtin swipl's

Arms, a build each, the rule taken out (13). Each is red in repeat.pl,

- the retry's Redo and Exit, red in the trace alone;

The retry's arm was written wrong in the first round: it answered 0 and

place left drops it. Written and taken out: a test that the walk
answered, `r == 1`. The frame being there says it, since a walk that

## numbervars/3,4 as swipl's (3.40.0)

swipl's numbervars/4 is foreign (pl-prims.c), and numbervars/3 is the clause
boot/syspred.pl writes over it, `numbervars(Term, From, To) :-
numbervars(Term, From, To, [])`, so the errors of both name numbervars/4.
Through 3.39.0 cocolog had neither, and a call raised existence_error. A
minor: the builtins are new.

- The row (lib/builtins.cicili, `coco_b_numbervars`) binds each distinct
  variable of the term to `'$VAR'(N)`, N counted up from the start, in the
  order term_variables/2 meets them (`coco_b_collect_vars`, a cycle's too),
  and unifies End with the next N. numbervars/3 is the builtins' Prolog
  half's clause, and the row of `*error-contexts*` (lib/solve.cicili) names
  numbervars/4, so both raise with `context(system:numbervars/4, _)`.
- The start: unbound, an instantiation error; an integer; a float with an
  integer's value, under 9.2e18 in magnitude (`1.0`, `-2.0`, `-0.0`);
  anything else type_error(integer, S) -- `1.5`, `1r2`, `'1'`, `1.0e30`,
  an infinity, a NaN, `f(1)`.
- The options are swipl's scan_options(): a proper list, a partial one an
  instantiation error and an improper one type_error(list, Tail); each
  element Name(Value), Name = Value with an atom for its name, or the bare
  atom `singletons`, and anything else type_error(option, E), an unbound
  element an instantiation error; an unknown name is passed by, and the
  last of a name holds. singletons(B) takes true, false, on, off, 1 and 0,
  else type_error(bool, B); functor_name(A) an atom, `[]` among them, else
  type_error(atom, A); attvar(A) an atom in the scan and then skip, bind or
  error, else domain_error(numbervar_option, Options), the whole list.
  cocolog has no attributed variable, so the action is only checked.
- singletons(true): each variable met once in the term's tree is bound to
  `'$VAR'('_')` and takes no number. A shared subterm counts at each place
  it stands, so a DAG is walked as the tree it stands for, as swipl's walk
  counts it (forty levels of one run for ever in both); a cyclic term marks
  none, as swipl's.
- The order of the questions is swipl's: the start's type, the options,
  the attvar action, the start's range against min_tagged_integer and
  max_tagged_integer (else representation_error(tagged_integer)), and then
  each number as it is given. So the end may pass the bound by one:
  `numbervars(f(_), Max, E)` gives E = Max + 1, and `numbervars(f(_, _),
  Max, _)` raises at the second variable. A singleton takes no number, and
  raises nothing.

THE TRACER WRITES A GOAL AS print/1 WRITES IT (`coco_write_print` in
`coco_trace_port`, and in the Redo's text, `coco_trace_paint` in
lib/solve-control.cicili), as swipl's debugger writes it, with portray, so
numbervars, and quoted: `'$VAR'(0)` is `A`, and a quote in an atom swipl's
`'don\'t'`. Through 3.39.0 it wrote the engine's own quoted text
(`coco_write_term`): no numbervars, and the doubled quote. A window's
recorded text, the journal and a backtrace keep the engine's quoted text:
the recorder's text is matched, not read.

test/files/numbervars.pl, new: 144 lines, swipl 9.0.4's byte for byte
(3.39.0 differs at line 3). It holds:
- the answers: a plain term, a ground one, a variable, a partial list, the
  order of first occurrence, depth first; a start other than 0, a negative
  one, a float with an integer's value and -0.0; a term that already holds

  compound and as a variable of the term; the bindings undone on

- what the writers make of the result: print/1, writeq/1, write/1 and
  write_canonical/1, the letters past Z (`Y`, `Z1`, `A2`) and a negative
  number (`S_1`), a singleton's `_`, a functor name's own terms, format/2's
  ~w, ~q and ~p, and write_term/2 with numbervars(true) and

- the options: singletons in every form (on, off, 1, 0, the bare name,

- the errors, each in swipl's order: the start's, the tagged bound (each

- determinism: neither leaves a choice point; clause/2 shows numbervars/3's

test/trace.pl: five queries over test/trace-program.pl's `nv/1`, `nw/0`,
`nq/0`, `nr/1` and `ns/1`, held to swipl's ports (113 checks): numbervars/3's
call is a port and numbervars/4 under it none, a failure at its end is its
Fail, and a goal is written as print/1 writes it, at a port and in a retry's
Redo. library/flow/modes.pl:
numbervars/3 and /4 are det, and the tables are rebuilt. The dialect card's

Not swipl's (COMPAT.md): a start between swipl's max_tagged_integer, 2^56-1

## predicate_property/2 as swipl's (3.41.0)

swipl's predicate_property/2 (boot/syspred.pl) lists a predicate's
properties in the order of its '$predicate_property'/2 clauses, and answers
a system or library predicate's from what its definition says: built_in,
imported_from(system), nodebug, iso, a meta_predicate(Spec), and so on.
Through 3.40.0 cocolog answered every builtin `visible`, `built_in`,
`foreign`, `static` and `defined`, a library's clauses as the program's own
(no imported_from, no meta_predicate, no built_in for one swipl writes in
C), none of the program's file, line, meta_predicate or ssu, and raised
type_error(callable, H) of a head that is no callable term. A minor: the
answers are new.

- THE TABLE (lib/swipl-props.cicili, 849 rows, generated by
  tools/props/tables.pl under the reference swipl 9.0.4 from
  `predicate_property(system:H, P)` and the library modules' exports):
  each row a name, an arity, swipl's imported_from and implementation
  module, a word of flags (built_in, foreign, transparent, nodebug,
  noprofile, iso, ssu, notrace, non_terminal, public, dynamic, multifile)
  and the meta arguments a character each. `coco-emit-swipl-props`
  (lib/builtins.cicili) makes it one function, a cond an arity and a strcmp
  a row, as the ISO table is.
- THE WALK (`coco_b_pred_props`, lib/builtins-db.cicili): a construct, a
  C row and a library's clauses the program gave none of its own answer
  from the table, but non_terminal, which is a grammar rule a read
  translated for every predicate (swipl's system non-terminals are the two
  DCG libraries', which cocolog reads from swipl's files: the table's bit
  was an arm green everywhere); what it has no row for -- the program's
  own, or cocolog's -- from its declarations: built_in and nodebug for a
  construct or a C row, public, non_terminal, dynamic, volatile, thread_local,
  multifile, discontiguous, imported_from(M) of a module/2 read's (`pmod`),
  transparent for module_transparent/1 or a meta argument a module is
  given to, meta_predicate(Spec) (`pmeta`, noted by the directive,
  `coco_pred_meta_note`), nodebug under generate_debug_info false, ssu for
  a single-sided one. FOREIGN is cocolog's own model: what listing/1 writes
  as `%   Foreign:` and clause/2 refuses to show has no clauses to count;
  the rest is interpreted, with its counts. A head that is no callable term
  fails, as swipl's.
- implementation_module(M) of a head named is `'$pred_impl'/2`, as swipl's
  property_predicate/2 answers it before the walk: the table's module, a
  module/2 read's, `system` for cocolog's own C, `user` for the program's
  and for a name nothing defines.
- FILE(F) AND LINE_COUNT(L): the first clause a file read
  (`pfile`/`pline` on the predicate, noted at a read's first sight of it in
  `coco_reload_for`, the path interned once a file, an included file's a
  path of its own). Each the predicate's first file's, the line moving when
  that file is read again, kept across a retract of the first clause --
  swipl's chain keeps the erased clause first until its collector reclaims
  it -- and none after an asserta/1, whose clause no file read, or
  abolish/1. A library's
  too, as swipl's, where cocolog read it from a file: the eight of
  lib/swipl/ are swipl 9.0.4's files byte for byte, so their names and
  lines are swipl's (but dcg_basics.pl and dcg_high_order.pl for swipl's
  dcg/basics.pl and dcg/high_order.pl). A library found through a relative
  library path is named by its absolute path (`lb_load_pl`): through 3.40.0
  `./library` on the path named library(async) `library/async.pl`, in its
  reports too.

test/files/predicate_property.pl, new: 170 lines, swipl 9.0.4's byte for
byte (3.40.0 differs at line 2). It holds:
- the program's predicates of every kind -- consulted, dynamic, declared
  and nothing else, discontiguous, multifile, public, module_transparent,
  meta_predicate, thread_local, volatile, a non-terminal, single-sided,
  under generate_debug_info false, asserted, a module's the program loaded
  and a system name the program defines itself -- their whole walk, less
  what describes how swipl stores a predicate, the file named by its base;
- 55 system predicates and 26 library predicates, less what each says of
  its own implementation;
- a head that is no callable term, a property of none, a name nothing
  defines, the qualifiers, implementation_module(M), foreign and
  interpreted where both write a predicate alike, and the program's own
  predicates that have a property, the head unbound;
- file/1 and line_count/1 after an asserta/1, an assertz/1 and a retract of
  the first clause, in a multifile predicate's two files, in a file read
  again as it changes, in an included file and after it, and the
  meta_predicate declaration an abolish/1 takes;
- the vendored libraries' files and lines.

test/engine.pl's `own_properties`: call_metered/4, which swipl has none
of, is built_in, foreign, static and nodebug, its module system's; an
assoc helper's module is assoc's; library(async), found through a relative
library path, names its absolute file. test/reconsult.pl's `abolished`:
abolish/1 takes the file and the meta arguments predicate_property/2 told
of. library/flow/modes.pl: '$pred_impl'/2 is semidet, the tables rebuilt.

Not swipl's (COMPAT.md): size(N), last_modified_generation(G) and
indexed(I) are never answered; foreign and the counts of a predicate the
two write differently are cocolog's own implementation's; a library
compiled into cocolog (lists, apply, error) has no file; after
`abolish(p/1), assertz(p(x))` swipl's names the abolished clause's file
until its collector reclaims it, cocolog's none; a walk with the head
unbound covers the program's own predicates, as current_predicate/1's;
the hooks swipl declares dynamic in user (term_expansion/2) are no
predicate until the program gives one a clause.

Arms, a build each, the rule taken out (40). Each is red in
predicate_property.pl, test/engine.pl's `own_properties` or
test/reconsult.pl, and the arm of no edit is green in all three:

- the table at all; built_in from it, and from a construct or a C row
  where it has no row (red in engine alone);
- foreign of a library's clauses swipl writes in C, and of a construct or
  a C row; interpreted, and the clause counts, only where not foreign;
- imported_from from the table and from a module/2 read; transparent from
  the table and from a meta argument; meta_predicate from the table, the
  program's own, and its note at the directive;
- file and line: shown at all, noted at all, the first file's kept, the
  line moving on a re-read, the path made once a file (red over an
  included file), a library's noted, asserta/1 taking them, abolish/1
  taking the meta arguments and the file (red in reconsult alone: at first
  by a parse error of the answer's unquoted path, and the check writes it
  with writeq/1 since);
- nodebug from the table, of a construct or a C row (engine alone) and
  under generate_debug_info false; noprofile; notrace; ssu from the table
  and of a single-sided rule; iso;
- a head that is no callable term failing;
- implementation_module's clause, the table's module, a module/2 read's,
  a library helper's (engine alone), user for a name nothing defines;
- a library found through a relative path named by its absolute path
  (engine alone).

The table's non_terminal bit was green in all three: the mark a read
leaves on a grammar rule gives every non-terminal swipl's system has, the
two DCG libraries', which cocolog reads from swipl's files. The bit is no
longer read. Written and taken out before the arms, as nothing could make
them red: the table's public (two rows, neither a predicate cocolog has),
an iso answer for what the table has no row for (every ISO predicate is

meta_predicate, transparent and file.

The cost, callgrind (tools/flow/zero.sh, work less padding, 3.40.0 to

lookup 48 043 540 to 48 044 748. The step loop is not touched; the counts

the implementation_module clause of the builtins' Prolog half, read at

Narrow cases green: lint, files (122 cases, each agreeing with swipl),

## current_predicate/1 named whole as swipl's (3.42.0)

swipl's current_predicate/1 asks of the module it is called in, user's for
a program: a predicate of swipl's system is user's through its import of
system, and a library module's export is user's once the program imported
it -- append/3 is none until a load names library(lists), whose module
swipl has not even read before that. Through 3.41.0 cocolog answered from
what defines the name: a construct or a C row yes from the start,
aggregate_all/3, nth0/3 and listing/1 among them, and a library's clauses
never, between/3, sub_atom/5, bagof/3 and numbervars/3 among them, and
member/2 after use_module(library(lists)). A minor: the answers are new.

- THE PROGRAM'S OWN FIRST (`coco_pred_current`, lib/kb.cicili): a clause
  or a declaration of its own answers yes, whatever its name; what a
  construct, a C row or a library's clauses define is then asked of the
  builtins module's hook (`coco_b_cp_current`, lib/builtins-db.cicili,
  installed by cocolog.cicili beside the dwim hook; null in a test binary,
  where a construct or a C row answers as through 3.41.0). By
  lib/swipl-props.cicili's table (3.41.0's): a predicate whose module is
  system or a `$` one is user's, wherever cocolog defines it; one of a
  library module's (lists, apply, assoc, ...) once the program imported
  it; one the table has no row for -- cocolog's own -- what a construct or
  a C row of it says: call_metered/4 is current, library(async)'s go/1 and
  library(llm)'s llm_chat/3 are not. A read's `:- if(current_predicate(N/A))`
  asks the same function (`coco_cond_eval`).
- WHAT THE PROGRAM IMPORTED (`coco_imp_note`; a process-wide list, as
  swipl's module user is, of rows: the module, and all of it, one name, all
  but a group's names, or a name so excepted): each load of library(Name)
  the program's read or goal makes -- use_module/1, use_module/2 with its
  import list or its except/1, ensure_loaded/1, autoload/2's list
  (autoload/1 imports nothing, as swipl's), a list of files, consult/1,
  `[File]`, load_files/2 with its imports(I) -- noted BEFORE the load, as
  the goal is read nowhere after it (a load may collect the heap). The load
  directives through `coco_import_hook` in `coco_directive`, the goals in
  `lb_use` and `lb_load_file` (lib/library.cicili: `lb_import_note`,
  `lb_import_lf`). A library's own read imports nothing: a load is the
  program's where the store is not muted or the load is its own
  (`lb-load-is-ours`, `ownload`). The module by swipl's name for it:
  dcg/basics is dcg_basics, dcg/high_order dcg_high_order, listing
  prolog_listing. A load of a library no table names notes a module none of
  whose predicates the table has, so it imports nothing; a library the
  table names is always there.
- predicate_property/2 OF A HEAD IT NAMES IMPORTS IT (`'$pp_autoload'/1`),
  as swipl's define_or_generate/1 autoloads a library's export into user,
  for any property but the six swipl's property_predicate/2 answers
  without (visible, undefined, iso, built_in, autoload(_),
  implementation_module(_)), and into user's module alone: of

## sum_list/2, max_list/2, min_list/2 and the set predicates as swipl's rules (3.42.1)

swipl 9.0.4's library(lists) writes sum_list/3 (under sum_list/2),
max_list/2,3, min_list/2,3, subtract/3, intersection/3, union/3 and
subset/2 as single-sided rules, `([], ...)` and `([X|Xs], ...)`, so a list
no rule matches -- no list, an unbound one, the end of a partial one --
raises existence_error(matching_rule, lists:Name(...)) at the tail the walk
reached, with context(lists:Name/Arity, _), after the elements before it
were taken. Through 3.42.0 cocolog's folds failed for any list but a proper
one, before they read an element, and the four set predicates, plain
clauses, failed for a list that was none and enumerated an unbound one
(`subtract(L, [a], R)` gave L = [], then [a], then [a, a], R = [] each
time, without end). A patch, as 3.26.1's max_member/2 was.

- THE SET PREDICATES are swipl's text (lib/lists.cicili's Prolog half):
  `subtract([E|T], D, R) => ( memberchk(E, D) -> subtract(T, D, R) ; R =
  [E|R1], subtract(T, D, R1) )`, and so on. Each commits at its head, as
  the old clauses committed at their cut.
- max_list/2 AND min_list/2 are swipl's two rules each, the second
  `max_list([], _) => fail`, so `max_list(foo, M)` raises
  lists:max_list(foo, _), named lists:max_list/2.
- THE FOLDS' C WALKS ASK THE TAIL WHERE THEY END (`coco_l_sum`,
  `coco_l_extreme`): [] ends the walk, anything else raises
  existence_error(matching_rule, lists:sum_list(Tail, Acc, Sum)), named
  lists:sum_list/3 (`coco_l_no_rule`, through `coco_m_raise_pi`: the walk's
  own errors name system:(is)/2, as swipl's arithmetic does). Acc is what
  the elements before the tail made -- `sum_list([1, 2|foo], S)` names 3,
  `max_list([1, 3|_], M)` names 3 -- and an element before the tail is
  evaluated first, so `sum_list([a|foo], S)` raises type_error(evaluable,
  a/0). Through 3.42.0 a length call in front of each refused any list but
  a proper one; a list that is its own tail still fails, past as many steps
  as the heap has cells, where swipl's rules walk it for ever (COMPAT.md).

test/files/lists_ssu.pl, new: 75 lines, swipl 9.0.4's byte for byte (3.42.0
differs at line 8). It holds each predicate's answers on proper lists (an
expression and a rational summed, a float picked over an equal integer, an
atom taken as the first element, bound outputs that hold and that do not),
each kind of list no rule matches with the accumulator named, the errors of
an element before the tail, memberchk/2's error over a second argument that
is no list, sumlist/2 naming sum_list/3, and each leaving no choice point
on a proper list. test/cyclic.pl's lists part: the three folds fail of a
list of numbers that is its own tail.

Arms, a build each, the rule taken out (13). Each is red in lists_ssu.pl or
test/cyclic.pl, and the arm of no edit is green in both and in
max_member.pl:

- the sum's walk asking its tail, and max_list/2's and min_list/2's;
- the accumulator the raise names: the sum so far, the best so far (red
  where the input's was named);
- the raise's context, lists:sum_list/3 (red as the walk's own
  system:(is)/2), and its goal's qualifier, lists: (red bare);
- max_list/2's second rule, and min_list/2's (red as a plain clause:
  `max_list(foo, M)` failed);
- subtract/3, intersection/3, union/3 and subset/2 as rules, each (red as
  its 3.42.0 clauses);
- the walks' count of the heap's cells (red in cyclic: a list of numbers
  that is its own tail walked for ever, and the case's child was killed at
  its minute).

The cost, callgrind. The step loop is not touched: tools/flow/zero.sh,
work less padding, 3.42.0 to 3.42.1, nrev 65 894 633 to 65 903 896, queens
40 277 153 to 40 275 102, lookup 48 045 965 to 48 052 721. Each
function's own cost, the program less its run of no rep, says where: the
arrays and tables a run starts with are larger by the start's reading, and
grow at other points. On nrev every function of the engine does the same
work to the instruction, and one realloc more copies the heap (libc's
memcpy +8 488, malloc and free +775); on queens the heap grows once less
(coco_grow_slow, coco_stack_cap and their callers -87, libc -1 966); on
lookup the
table of compiled codes grows once less (coco_clause_code -1 748,
coco_code_put -940) and, larger, is cleared at a compaction (libc's memset
+8 876).
A start (`cocolog query true`) is 35 086 097 instructions and 35 190 695
(+104 598, 0.3 %): the longer rule texts read, put and compiled
(coco_cbody_n +13 557, coco_store_put_node +10 943, coco_intern_len
+10 307, coco_functor_id +7 695). A call, 2 000 of each less the same loop
with none: sum_list/2 of a list of 100 numbers 12 998 instructions and
8 447 (-35 %: the list is walked once, where 3.42.0 measured its length
first), max_list/2 13 599 and 10 548 (-22 %); of a list of ten atoms and
[b, d, f], subtract/3 28 658 and 27 880 (-2.7 %), intersection/3 28 993
and 26 172 (-9.7 %), union/3 28 668 and 27 880 (-2.7 %); and subset/2 of
[b, d, f] in the ten 5 180 and 7 329 (+41 %). A rule set's catch-all
clause, `H :- '$ssu_none'(M, H)`, is a second candidate: each call of a
rule pushes a choice point its cut takes, and leaves the register call
(coco_select_clause, coco_pred_next_clause, cc_head_ssu and the construct
of the cut), where swipl raises from the machine. A lead, not done: the
raise made by the clause selection when an SSU predicate's last candidate

Narrow cases green: lint, files (124 files, each agreeing with swipl),

## Two regressions of 3.42.0: the store warmed at start-up, and the import list freed twice (3.42.2)

CI went red on 3.42.0 (run 42382968541), and on 3.42.1 for the same two
reasons; neither case was among 3.42.0's narrow ones.

- **test/tunnel.pl, on all three jobs.** A reader behind the stand-in
  edge, whose certificate does not carry the name it asked for, said
  `fetching predicates` where it says `fetching clauses`, and the process
  ended 3 where it ends 2. 3.42.0's `coco_pred_current` warmed the store
  before it answered a name cocolog defines in C, and library(assoc)'s
  `:- if(current_predicate('$btree_find_node'/5))`, read at every start,
  made the Zeytun backend fetch the store's predicate list before the
  program's first goal: the refusal ended the start, not the goal. A name
  cocolog defines in C that the hook calls current answers before the
  store is asked again, as through 3.41.0 a C row did: the program's own
  could only say yes again. A name the hook calls no predicate of the
  program's (nth0/3 before an import of library(lists)) still asks the
  store whether the program defined it, and the hook is asked once.
- **test/cowork.pl, on the Linux job.** `double free or corruption
  (!prev)`. What the program imported (3.42.0's `coco_imp_note`) is one
  list for the process, as swipl's module user is one, and a
  library(thread) thread or a green world's worker loads with a machine of
  its own: each load added its row with no lock, and two loads at once
  grew the array with realloc(3) and freed it twice. The list's four
  statics are held by one mutex, `cp_imp_mx`, taken by every reader and
  writer -- `coco_imp_note`, the hook's lookup (`coco_b_cp_current`) and
  '$pp_autoload'/1's, whose test and add are one step under it.

test/thread.pl's new section `imports`: eight threads load library(lists)
3 000 times each, use_module/1 and use_module/2 with an import list by
turns, and ask current_predicate(append/3) after each load. On 3.42.1 a
program of the same loads ended the process in every one of six runs on
the four-core Linux box (`realloc(): invalid old size`, `double free or
corruption (!prev)`, segmentation faults), and the case in two of three;
on 3.42.2 the program is green in five runs and the case in six. tunnel
is red on 3.42.1 and green on 3.42.2, and cowork green in six runs.

Arms, a build each, the rule taken out (2), and the arm of no edit green
in tunnel, thread (three runs) and cowork (three runs):

- the C row answered before the store is asked: red in tunnel alone, with
  CI's two failures (`a name the certificate does not carry is refused`,

- the lock: test/thread.pl aborted in six of eight runs, and the program
  of loads in ten of ten.

The hook asked once is a guard of cost: the first cut asked it again after

dearer than 3.42.1's.

## nth0/3 and nth1/3 over a partial list, and lists past the stack limit, as swipl's (3.42.3)

swipl 9.0.4's nth0/3 and nth1/3 with the index given walk the list with
'$seek_list'/4 and hand what is left to nth0_det/3, whose head binds an
unbound tail: `nth0(1, L, a)` is L = [_, a|_], `nth0(3, [a|T], X)` binds
T = [_, _, X|_], once. Through 3.42.2 cocolog's C row failed wherever its
walk met an unbound tail -- the one difference left after 3.42.1 by a scan
of every export of swipl's library(lists) over each shape a list takes. A
patch, as 3.42.1 was.

- THE WALK BINDS THE TAIL IT MEETS (`coco_l_nth_at`, lib/lists.cicili): the
  cells it had still to pass, fresh, and the element's, then a fresh tail,
  built as length/2's completion builds its cells (`coco_push_struct`, each
  linked by its tail) and unified with the tail once. A tail that is
  anything else -- `[]`, `foo` -- fails, as before.
- A LIST TOO LONG FOR THE STACK LIMIT RAISES BEFORE IT IS BUILT
  (`coco-l-too-long`, a DEFMACRO): list cells whose bytes alone pass the
  machine's limit raise error(resource_error(stack), _) -- nth0/3's and
  nth1/3's tail, length/2's completion, numlist/3 -- as swipl's length/2
  raises at once. A growth past the limit is given and stops the engine
  only at its next step (3.32.0), so a C loop never saw it: through 3.42.2
  `length(L, 1000000000000)` built until the kernel killed the process, and
  the new nth0/3 would have. A list the limit could hold is built, and the
  step after asks what the stacks hold, as before. swipl's nth0/3 and
  numlist/3 are Prolog and build such a list a step at a time, for ever
  where its collector takes the cells nobody holds (COMPAT.md).
- numlist/3's count with no limit (COCOLOG_STACK_LIMIT=0): 2^64 cells
  wrapped to 0 and answered [], and a count past what an array's bytes can
  say wrapped them (2^62 + 1 cells asked for 8 bytes and wrote past them);
  each raises resource_error(memory) before anything is allocated, and an
  array malloc(3) refuses raises it too, where through 3.42.2 the call
  failed.

test/files/nth_open.pl, new: 48 lines, swipl 9.0.4's byte for byte (3.42.1
fails at its first line, and on its length/2 line built until the kernel
killed it). It holds nth0/3 and nth1/3 over an unbound list, a partial one
and one that ends in `foo`, `[]` or too soon, an index past the end of
those; the element shared with the caller; the index's errors; each answer
deterministic; and length/2 of a count no stack holds raising
resource_error(stack). swipl 9.0.4 itself crashes (SIGSEGV) on
`length([a, b|_], 9223372036854775807)`, which the file leaves out.
test/engine.pl's `own_too_long` holds what swipl never answers: nth0/3,
nth1/3 and numlist/3 past the limit raising at once, a list the limit holds
built, and with no limit a count no array can hold, and one malloc(3)
refuses, raising resource_error(memory), checked in a child.

Arms, a build each, the rule taken out (10), each red in nth_open.pl or
test/engine.pl's `own_too_long`, the arm of no edit green in both and in
lists_ssu.pl; the arms run under `ulimit -v 2500000`:

- the unbound tail bound at all (red in both); the element's cell
  (nth_open); the count of cells, the element's beside the cells passed

- the limit asked of nth0/3's and nth1/3's tail (engine), of length/2's

- numlist/3's count past what an array's bytes can say (engine), and its

The cost, callgrind, 3.42.2 to 3.42.3. The step loop is not touched

40 275 120 and 40 275 127, lookup 48 052 661 on both). A start (`cocolog

## call/N in the structure of a search's goal is `'<meta-call>'/1`'s, as swipl's (3.43.0)

swipl 9.0.4's findall/3, findall/4, bagof/3, setof/3, forall/2 and
aggregate_all/3 are clauses that meta-call their goal, as
'$execute_directive_3' runs a directive and `swipl -g` its goal under
catch/3, and '$run_init_goal'/1 an initialization goal: a goal that is a
control structure is compiled into a `'<meta-call>'/1` frame, and call/N in
it is compiled in place (I_USERCALL), so what call/N's goal raises -- an
unknown procedure, a goal that is no goal -- names `'<meta-call>'/1`.
Through 3.42.3 cocolog ran every call/N at a search's root as a frame of
its own: `findall(x, (true, call(foo, a)), _)` raised
`context(system:call/2, _)` where swipl's is
`context(system:'<meta-call>'/1, _)`. Found by the scan of the vendored
libraries' exports against swipl, in the shapes library(yall) and
library(aggregate) hand findall/3. A minor: a caught error's context
changes.

- WHERE A call/N STANDS IN ITS SEARCH'S GOAL (`coco_root_part`,
  lib/solve-control.cicili): a call/N whose word has no owner -- a part of
  a structure at a search's root -- is asked where it stands in the goal by
  the walk the unknown procedure's context makes (`coco_query_walk`, by the
  names' ids since: it compared each name with strcmp(3)). A part of a
  structure is compiled in place; the goal itself is call/N's own frame,
  and the argument of once/1, ignore/1, not/1 or catch/3 is meta-called
  afresh, as swipl's are; and a call/N a variable of the structure was
  bound to as it ran is call/N's own (`coco_goal_was_var`), as swipl's
  compile met the variable.
- WHICH SEARCHES: findall/3 and its kin, forall/2, aggregate_all/3, a
  directive and `run FILE GOAL`, an initialization goal (`rootn` 1 to 3, 5
  and 6). A search C starts -- with_output_to/2, format/2's `~@` (4) -- and
  a query, a thread or an isolated run (0) keep call/N a frame of its own,
  as swipl's C starts a goal: with_output_to/2's structure is a
  `'<meta-call>'/1` for a plain goal and names call/N for call/N's, and
  swipl's thread_create/3 the same.
- THE ANSWER IS KEPT PER SEARCH for a cell of its goal, which stands below
  the search's start and no backtracking in it winds back: the engine's
  `rpg`, the cell over the answer's bit, and `rpc`, the heap's collections
  when it was asked, as a collection moves the cells -- so a call/N a loop
  of the search runs again walks the goal once. A goal the search built is
  walked each time.

test/files/meta_call_root.pl, new: 77 lines, swipl 9.0.4's byte for byte
(3.42.3 differs at 35 of them): call/N in each structure of findall/3's,
findall/4's, bagof/3's, setof/3's, aggregate_all/3's and forall/2's goal,
its goal no goal and qualified; call/N as the goal itself, under once/1,
ignore/1, not/1, catch/3 and a variable, and a plain goal under catch/3;
with_output_to/2's; and the cut, `$` and the answers that do not move.
test/directives.pl: a directive's, an initialization goal's and `run FILE

## The goals swipl's C calls, and the qualifier a meta-call strips, as swipl's (3.44.0)

swipl 9.0.4 calls some goals from C: with_output_to/2's, format/2's `~@`,
a thread's, sig_atomic/1's (setup_call_cleanup/3's setup) and the cleanup
handler's. callProlog() takes the goal's qualifiers off, calls a plain goal
in the frame `'$c_call_prolog'/0` names, and a control construct as the
system's predicate boot/init.pl defines for it -- `(G1, G2) :- call((G1,
G2))`, `\+ Goal :- \+ Goal`, `$(Goal) :- $(Goal)` -- with each argument
qualified by the caller's module. setup_call_cleanup/3's goal runs in
setup_call_catcher_cleanup/4's own frame (I_CALLCLEANUP). Through 3.43.0
cocolog called a plain goal of with_output_to/2's and `~@`'s so, but ran a
structure as a meta-call does: `with_output_to(S, (true, 1))` was
type_error(callable, (true, 1)) named with_output_to/2 where swipl's is
type_error(callable, (user:true, user:1)) named ','/2, `\+ foo` was named
`'<meta-call>'/1` where swipl's is (\+)/1, and `(fail ; call(foo))` named
call/1 where swipl's (;)/2 compiles call/N in place. setup_call_cleanup/3's
setup ran under once/1, its goal under catch/3 and its cleanup in
`'$cleanup_call'/3`, whose names their errors said, and a thread's goal
was a query's: a plain goal's error named nothing. A meta-call kept the
qualifier swipl strips: `call(lists:(\+ foo))` raised
existence_error(procedure, foo/0) where swipl's names `lists:foo/0`,
`call(lists:'$cut'(1))` succeeded, `findall(x, 1:foo, _)` named
`'<meta-call>'/1` where swipl's findall_loop/4 refuses it before it runs,
and `lists:call(foo)` written in a clause ran call/1 in place, its error
the clause's, where swipl's calls call/1, a frame of its own. When a goal
and its cleanup both raised, the goal's ball was raised and the cleanup's
dropped; swipl's raises the cleanup's where it is more urgent. Found going
on from 3.43.0's setup goal, left out there. A minor: a caught error's
context, and a ball, change.

- THE GOAL SWIPL'S C CALLS (`coco_c_root`, lib/solve-control.cicili): the
  qualifiers off; ','/2, (->)/2 and (*->)/2 called again as `(M:A, M:B)`,
  M the innermost module (user where none) and an argument qualified
  already its own; (;)/2 as `M:(A ; B)` where its arguments share M, else
  `M:(A ; N:B)`; `\+ M:X` and `$(M:X)` for M not user. A part is said of
  user only where that changes how it runs (`coco_c_arg`): a call/N, a
  control structure, a variable, what is no goal -- a plain goal under
  `user:` runs as it would bare, for a step of the `:` construct more.
  Its faults before it runs (`coco_c_root_fault`): an unbound or
  non-callable goal the starter's, named with_output_to/2 or format/3; a
  structure that is no goal the construct's own, its formal with every
  part said of its module (`coco_c_root_q`'s FULL),
  `type_error(callable, (user:true, user:1))` named ','/2.
  with_output_to/2, `~@`, a thread and an isolated run start their search
  there (`rootn` 4), and the walk an unknown procedure's context makes
  takes a root `\+ X` or `$(X)`'s X as theirs.
- `$/1` AT SUCH A ROOT (`coco_det_c_root`): G runs in ($)/1's frame, and
  its determinism error shows the goal that clause compiled,
  `determinism_error(call(user:fail), det, fail, goal)`, named
  `system:($)/1`.
- SETUP_CALL_CLEANUP/3 (the builtins' Prolog half): the setup through
  `'$c_goal'(S, 0, S1)`, a C half that makes a construct its system
  predicate's helper -- `'$c_and'/2`, `'$c_ite'/2`, `'$c_soft'/2`,
  `'$c_or'/2`, `'$c_not'/1`, `'$c_det'/1`, a part said of user as
  `coco_c_arg` says, every part where the structure is no goal -- and
  raises sig_atomic/1's error first for a setup unbound or no goal; the
  setup called in `'$c_call'/1`, once; the goal and the cleanup asked the
  same, setup_call_catcher_cleanup/4's errors (`'$c_goal'/3` kind 3); the
  goal in `'$scc_run'/1`; the cleanup through `'$c_goal'(C, 1, C1)`, a
  structure call/1's to compile (`'$c_call1'/1`). Each helper has a row of
  `*frame-contexts*` with swipl's name for its frame (`'$c_call_prolog'/0`,
  call/1, setup_call_catcher_cleanup/4, ','/2, ...). The checks were two
  clauses of the Prolog half through 3.43.0, each its own if-then-else.
- THE CLEANUP'S BALL REPLACES THE GOAL'S ONLY WHEN MORE URGENT
  (`'$scc_urgency'/2`): time_limit_exceeded over error(_, _) over any
  other ball, as swipl 9.0.4 ranks them (resource_error among the errors);
  the goal's where they are as urgent; never a ball raised after the goal
  exited (external_exception).
- A QUALIFIER ON CALL/N OR A STRUCTURE (`coco_colon_written`,
  lib/solve-loop.cicili, asked by the `:` construct, which tells `user` by
  its name, `coco_atom_is_user`). A meta-call's own goal -- its word META,
  a frame of swipl's own (call/N's goal, once/1's, catch/3's), a variable
  bound as it ran, a search's own goal -- is stripped, as I_USERCALL0
  strips it: MO said of each goal of the structure (`coco_colon_qualify`),
  call/N left in place with its goal MO's (`call(lists:foo)`), so what
  nothing defines is named `lists:foo/0`. Written in code that runs -- a
  clause, a part of a structure a meta-call compiled -- `M:call(G)` is
  call/N's own frame, `call(M:G)`, and a structure has M said of each
  goal. A variable goal is `call(M:X)`, as swipl compiles one; `$(G)` is
  never qualified inside, as its determinism error shows G as written
  (COMPAT.md).
- THE META-CALL'S CHECK (`coco_goal_check`, `coco_goal_leaves`) takes the
  root's qualifiers off -- `findall(x, 1:foo, _)` type_error(atom, 1) and
  `findall(x, _:foo, _)` an instantiation error, named by findall_loop/4
  before the goal runs -- and walks `M:G` in a structure:
  `call(lists:(true, 1:foo))` type_error(module, 1). So does the clause
  compiler's (`cc_bad_leaf`, lib/kb-compile.cicili), which keeps
  `once(lists:(true, 1))` written in a clause a term, for once/1 to raise
  type_error(callable, (true, 1)), as swipl's compile of the goal does.
- A CONSTRUCT'S NAME OF AN ARITY NO CONSTRUCT HAS is no construct under a
  qualifier (`coco_construct_pi`, emitted from `*callable-constructs*`):
  `lists:true(1)` is existence_error(procedure, lists:true/1), and
  `lists:'$cut'(1)`, a marker of the engine's, `lists:'$cut'/1`.
- A QUALIFIER MET IS A FLAG, NEVER A CELL (`qual`): a thread's goal is read
  into a machine of its own, where its module atom is heap cell 0, and the
  first cut, which tested the cell, lost `lists:` there
  (`thread_create(lists:(\+ foo), _)` named `'<meta-call>'/1`).

## A meta-predicate's arguments said of the module the call is made in, as swipl's (3.45.0)

swipl 9.0.4 qualifies each argument a meta_predicate/1 declaration marks
`0` to `9`, `:`, `^` or `//` with the module the call is made in, unless it
is a term `M:X` already, whatever M is (`1:foo`, `_:foo`): `p(foo)` of `:-
meta_predicate p(0).` runs as `p(user:foo)`, so a head `h(user:foo)`
matches `h(foo)` and a head `h(foo)` does not; `m:q(foo)` is `q(m:foo)`,
and so is call/N of a closure `m:q`. The module is the one of the clause
the call is written in -- a meta-predicate's own clause's its own module,
a module_transparent/1 predicate's its caller's -- and a directive's the
module of the file being read. A predicate called before its declaration
qualifies nothing: its first call built the code that calls it; and a
declaration made again is the one that stands (`rd(0)` then `rd(?)`
qualifies nothing). Through 3.44.0 cocolog noted the declaration for
predicate_property/2 alone and qualified nothing, so library(aggregate)'s
`aggregate(count, _, N)` -- swipl's instantiation error from
findall_loop/4, its goal `user:_` -- ran its unbound goal through
clean_body/2 to the stack limit, and an error named an argument as the
call wrote it: `lists:max_member(le, _, foo)` where swipl's names
`lists:max_member(user:le, _, foo)`, `assoc:map_assoc_(foo, integer)` and
`[_,_,_]>>true` where swipl's have `user:integer` and `user:true`
(COMPAT.md's row, now gone). Found by the scan of the vendored libraries'
exports over odd shapes: lists, assoc, pairs, ordsets, ugraphs, yall,
aggregate, dcg/basics and dcg/high_order, each export over a proper, an
unbound, a partial and an improper argument, up to four answers or the
ball; they agree with swipl now but for the context of
resource_error(stack), a dict in swipl's (COMPAT.md).

- THE STEP QUALIFIES (`coco_meta_qualify`, lib/solve-control.cicili) on
  its slow path, after the Call port: swipl's Call shows `p(foo)`, its
  Exit and its Fail `p(user:foo)`. A functor of such a predicate is never
  stamped a plain predicate (`fgen`), so each of its calls takes that path
  and the fast path asks nothing more. The slow path asks a bit the
  declaration sets (`pattrs` 512, `coco_pred_meta_note`) and calls the
  qualification out of line on a branch of its own (`coco_step_meta`):
  a plain predicate's slow path calls nothing it did not call through
  3.44.0 (below).
- THE MODULE (`coco_meta_ctx`): the module/2 read's that defined the
  clause the call is written in (`pmod`), user for a program's clause;
  where no clause is the goal's -- a directive's, a search's -- or the
  clause is a module_transparent/1 predicate's, the module of the read
  under way (`ssu_mod`), else user. M:G qualifies with M
  (`coco_meta_colon`, in `coco_colon`), library(aggregate)'s
  aggregate_all/3 too, whose goal swipl calls in M.
- CALLED BEFORE DECLARED: every predicate the slow path resolves is noted
  called (`pattrs` 128), and a declaration of one called and not yet
  qualifying qualifies nothing (256). A declaration made again sets 512
  as it now stands.
- library(lists)' max_member/3 and min_member/3 are meta-predicates, as
  swipl's; library(apply)'s are not, whose answers would not move.

test/files/meta_args.pl, new: 68 lines, swipl 9.0.4's byte for byte
(3.44.0 differs at 53 of them), over a module its fixture writes
(test/files.pl). test/trace.pl: five queries of a meta-predicate's ports,
`mp/1` of test/trace-program.pl and `mt1/1` and `mt2/1` of
test/trace-library.pl, and the Exit and Fail goals of four of them

THE STEP'S PRICE, FOUND BY ITS PLACE (tools/flow/zero.sh against 3.44.0,
work less padding). The first cut noted the predicate called, asked
whether it qualified (`strpbrk` over the spec) and called the
qualification inline in the slow path: nrev +0.153 %, queens -0.042 %,

an inference -- on the fast path, which the change did not touch. The
whole of it out of line, one call in the slow path: nrev +0.159 %,

cost the same (nrev +0.158 %), and 3.44.0's inline stamp in its place,

itself, not the new goal it hands back. Callgrind's instructions in the
loop showed it: the machine pointer, reloaded from the stack into `r8` --
`coco_pred_probe`'s fifth argument -- went to `rdi` with the call there,
and was loaded a second time before the probe, once an inference. Four
arguments in three orders (nrev +0.168 %, queens +0.232 %), the machine
itself the fifth (lookup +0.584 %), the whole slow path out of line
(nrev +0.314 %, lookup +0.792 %): none. On a branch of its own, by the

nrev 66 134 088 to 66 132 243 (-0.003 %), queens 40 275 211 to
40 254 061 (-0.053 %), lookup 48 043 059 to 48 031 727 (-0.024 %), the
binary as committed, cuts and all. A
call in the loop's slow path is a register of its fast path, wherever it
stands and whatever it takes.

WHAT A DECLARED PREDICATE'S CALL COSTS (callgrind against 3.44.0, 2 000
calls a probe; instructions a call). `mp(ok(1))` of `:- meta_predicate
mp(0).` 557 more: the step's slow path, the functor never stamped (181),
the new goal and its `user:ok(1)` (243), the module (60); `mp(user:ok(1))`,

`max_member(@<, _, [1,2,3])` 2 359 (it cost 8 553), library(aggregate)'s

maplist/2 calls 1 001 (13 888). `lists:ok(1)` pays 46 (`coco_meta_colon`),
and a plain predicate's call, maplist/2 and call/N of a plain closure
nothing. The start, `cocolog query true`, 87 612 more (+0.25 %): where
strcmp's strings fall, which an earlier build of the change moved 136 816
the other way. Every other inference count is 3.44.0's. THREE CUTS GOT
THERE, each measured on its own build. Both names a qualification makes
were interned at each call and the clause's predicate found by name:
`:`/2 and user/0 are interned once a machine beside the ids
(`*functor-names*`, `coco-is-colon`), the predicate read from its

1 327, max_member/3 3 478 to 2 929, aggregate/3 4 158 to 3 763). call/1
walked a qualified plain goal for `$/0`, which it cannot hold
(`coco_det_kq`: `mc(ok(1))` 1 327 to 1 201, max_member/3 2 929 to 2 681).
And a meta-call's `user:G` ran the `:` step, a frame and a dispatch,

## meta_predicate/1 as a goal, and a predicate's calls qualified as its declaration stood at its first call, as swipl's (3.46.0)

swipl 9.0.4's meta_predicate/1 is a predicate: `meta_predicate(p(0))`
declares p as the directive does, a conjunction left to right, and
refuses what it cannot take with the balls pl-proc.c's meta_declaration()
raises. Through 3.45.0 cocolog had the directive alone: the goal was an
unknown procedure, and the directive took any spec in silence --
`:- meta_predicate baz(x).` declared nothing and said nothing, where
swipl says `x' is no meta-argument specifier and that the directive
failed. And swipl's first call of a predicate builds the code that calls
it -- its supervisor, an S_MQUAL for each argument the declaration then
marked -- and keeps it till abolish/1, so a declaration made after a call
changes predicate_property/2's answer and nothing a call does: 3.45.0
read the spec at each call, and `meta_predicate p(?)` after a call of
`p(0)`'s ended the qualification, where swipl's goes on. Found writing
the goal's case.

- THE GOAL (`meta_predicate(S) :- '$declare'(7, S).`, the builtins'
  Prolog half, over `coco_bi_meta_decl` in lib/solve-db.cicili): the spec
  walked by `coco_pred_meta_check` (lib/kb-pred.cicili) -- a conjunction
  at its top left to right, never one under a qualifier; each head's
  qualifiers taken off where an atom names the module (`_:p(0)` is a
  head of (:)/2, as PL_strip_module leaves it); the head a callable term
  and no ISO predicate's, asked before its arguments; each argument in
  order an integer 0 to 9 within a C int, or `?`, `+`, `-`, `*`, `:`,
  `^` or `//`. The heads before a fault are declared, as swipl's stand.
  The fault is swipl's ball, named system:(meta_predicate)/1:
  instantiation_error, type_error(callable, H), permission_error(modify,
  static_procedure, PI), domain_error(meta_argument_specifier, A) of an
  integer or an atom that is none, type_error(meta_argument_specifier, A)
  of anything else, representation_error(int) past a C int; a
  specifier's with `0..9` in its context, as swipl's.
- THE DIRECTIVE: a spec the goal would refuse is the goal's, as op/3's
  is (`coco_directive`): its error where it stands and the failed
  directive, swipl's two reports. A head of no arguments is noted too
  (`meta_predicate zero`, its spec the atom).
- THE FIRST CALL (`pmq`, appended to the predicate): `pmeta` as it stood
  when a step first called the predicate (`pattrs` 128), the spec the
  step and `M:G` qualify by, and whether they do (512); after that call a
  declaration is predicate_property/2's alone. 3.45.0's `pattrs` 256
  (declared after a call) is gone: a predicate called before its
  declaration has no spec to qualify by. abolish/1 forgets the call
  (`coco_pred_undeclare`: `pattrs` 0, `pmq` freed), as swipl's drops the
  supervisor; and a declaration that sets 512 clears its functor's stamp
  (`fgen` 0): a call after abolish/1 stamped it a plain predicate, and a
  stamped goal never reaches the slow path that qualifies it -- 3.45.0
  had the hole too, found by the case's abolish/1 lines.

test/files/meta_goal.pl, new: 86 lines, swipl 9.0.4's byte for byte
(3.45.0 differs at 70 of them). test/directives.pl: a file of
meta_predicate directives swipl refuses, its stderr word for word
(`emetad`), and the heads before the fault declared. Not swipl's
(COMPAT.md): a head a module qualifies is user's, one namespace; and
meta_predicate/1 of a system predicate that is not ISO's is taken
whatever user has called, where swipl's makes a predicate of user's
before user has called the system's and refuses it after
(permission_error(redefine, built_in_procedure, PI)).

THE ARMS, one build each on the code as it stands, the rule taken out,
each red in meta_goal.pl or in test/directives.pl's new checks (19 of
19; the arm of no edit green in all three cases): the goal (G01), the
conjunction's walk (G02, meta_args.pl red too: its module's directive is
a conjunction), a head's atom qualifiers off (G03), an ISO predicate
refused (G04) and before its arguments (G05), a C int (G06), 0 to 9
(G07), the atoms that are specifiers (G08), a type error for anything
else (G09), an instantiation error for an unbound argument (G10), `0..9`
in a specifier's context (G11), the heads before a fault declared (G12),
a refused directive the goal's (G13, red in directives alone), a head of
no arguments noted (G14) and its spec the atom (G15), the step's spec
decided before the first call alone (G16, meta_args.pl red too: 3.45.0's
late declaration), the step reading it (G17), abolish/1 forgetting the
call (G18) and the stamp cleared (G19). Under the runner's 2.5 GB
`ulimit -v`, test/directives.pl's seven checks of a halt under an
embedded store fail in every arm and in the binary as committed alike;
each arm is read by the checks it fails past those seven. A check the
first arms showed weak was made strong: `qux(0)` stands in the failed
directive's text too, so the declared spec is written with a marker.

THE COST, callgrind, 3.45.0 to 3.46.0. The step loop is not touched

Narrow cases green, each alone on the binary as committed: lint, reason,

## What the builtins ask of their arguments, and in what order, as swipl's (3.47.0)

A scan of the 211 builtins cocolog and swipl 9.0.4 both define, each
argument in turn given each of fifteen shapes -- unbound, `a`, `'A b'`,
`''`, 1, 0, -1, 3.5, a string, `[a,b]`, `[a|_]`, `[a|b]`, `[]`, `f(x)`,
`f(_,_)` -- the others unbound, and each goal's first four answers or its
ball set beside swipl's (7 229 goals), differed in 84 places through
3.46.0. Twelve of them were cocolog asking of an argument what swipl does
not ask, or asking it in another order; 3.47.0 asks as swipl asks, and
the scan differs in 59 places, listed at the end. Two more were found
writing the case: an option said twice, and a read's `Name = Value`.

- THE LIST'S END IS NO LEAF OF A STRUCTURE (`coco_goal_leaves`' `inner`,
  lib/solve-control.cicili). swipl compiles a meta-call's control
  structure before it runs any of it, and its compiler refuses `[]` where
  a goal stands: `call((true, []))`, `([] -> true)`, `\+ []`, `$([])`,
  `(true ; [])` and `[]@user` are type_error(callable, G) of the whole,
  where `call([])` alone, its qualifiers off, runs []/0 and raises its
  existence error. Through 3.46.0 every one of them ran []/0, and `(true ;
  [])` succeeded by its first branch. G@M's goal is compiled, never called
  alone (`coco_goal_check` walks it as an inner part), and findall/3,
  forall/2, aggregate_all/3 and a C-called structure (`(user:true,
  user:[])`) refuse it in their own names, as swipl's do.
- SETUP_CALL_CLEANUP/3 ASKS AS I_CALLCLEANUP ASKS (`'$c_goal'/3`'s kind 4,
  the builtins' Prolog half): the setup run, then the cleanup asked -- an
  unbound one instantiation_error, one that is no goal type_error(callable,
  C), `[]` among them -- before its frame is pushed, and the goal asked in
  that frame (`'$scc_run'/1`), so a goal that is none is an exception the
  cleanup runs for: `setup_call_cleanup(true, 1, out(c1))` prints c1 and
  raises type_error(callable, 1). Through 3.46.0 the goal was asked before
  the cleanup, the cleanup never ran for it, and a cleanup of `[]` ran
  []/0. call_cleanup/2 and setup_call_catcher_cleanup/4 with it.
- FORALL/2'S CONDITION RUNS BEFORE ITS ACTION IS ASKED (`coco_b_forall`):
  swipl's `\+ (call(C), \+ call(A))` asks the action only once the
  condition has an answer, so `forall(fail, _)` and `forall(fail, 1)`
  hold, `forall(nope, _)` is nope/0's existence error, and
  `forall((out(cond2) ; out(cond3)), 1)` prints cond2 and raises
  type_error(callable, 1). The condition then runs alone as `(C, true)`,
  to its first answer. Through 3.46.0 the action was asked first.
- FUNCTOR/3 ASKS THE NAME BEFORE THE ARITY (pl-prims.c's order,
  lib/solve-text.cicili): with the term unbound, an unbound name is
  instantiation_error, a compound one type_error(atomic, N) (`f(x)`, `[a|b]`,
  `"ab"` under codes), and only then an unbound arity instantiation_error;
  through 3.46.0 the arity was asked first.
- CURRENT_OP/3'S PRIORITY IS 1 TO 1200 (`coco_b_op_spec`,
  lib/builtins-db.cicili): `current_op(0, _, _)` is
  domain_error(operator_priority, 0), as swipl's; 3.46.0 failed.
- STRING_BYTES/3'S `[]` IS AN ENCODING THAT IS NONE: domain_error(encoding,
  []), as `'[]'`'s is; through 3.46.0 type_error(atom, []).
- AGGREGATE_ALL/3'S `[]` IS NO TEMPLATE: type_error(aggregate_template,
  []), swipl's invalid_template/1's, where an atom that names no aggregate
  is domain_error(aggregate_template, A); 3.46.0 said the domain error.
- DCG_TRANSLATE_RULE/2 OF A CLAUSE THAT CAN BE NONE FAILS
  (`coco_dcg_bi_rule`, lib/dcg.cicili): with the rule unbound, a clause
  neither unbound nor `_ :- _` (`a`, `[]`, `f(x)`) matches no clause of
  swipl's and fails; 3.46.0 raised instantiation_error, as it still does
  where the clause can be one.
- META_PREDICATE/1 FAILS AT THE LIST'S END (`coco_pred_meta_head`'s 8,
  lib/kb-pred.cicili): `meta_predicate([])`, `(m1(0), [])` and `([],
  m2(0))` fail -- swipl's meta_declaration() finds no procedure for `[]`
  -- the heads before it declared; 3.46.0 succeeded, and declared what
  came after the `[]` too.
- REDEFINE_SYSTEM_PREDICATE/1 TAKES USER'S DEFINITION AWAY FIRST
  (`coco_bi_redefine_system`, lib/solve-db.cicili), as pl-proc.c's
  abolishProcedure() does before it marks the predicate: the program's
  clauses by the walk abolish/1 takes (a library's predicate keeps the
  library's), then its declarations, so after `assertz(rd(1))` and
  `redefine_system_predicate(rd(_))` a call of rd/1 is an unknown
  procedure and the predicate no longer dynamic. Through 3.46.0 they
  stood.
- EXPAND_TERM/2 IS SWIPL'S EXPAND_TERMS/5 (`'$expand_terms'/3`,
  lib/dcg.cicili): a list is its terms, each expanded as a term is -- a
  rule into its declaration and its clause, term_expansion/2 asked of each
  -- a list among what they give spliced in (`[[a], [], [b, [c]]]` is `[a,
  [], b, c]`), and a partial or improper list type_error(list, L), the one
  a hook gives too. Through 3.46.0 a list was one term, no rule in it
  translated.
- TERM_STRING/3'S OPTIONS ARE MERGED AS SWIPL MERGES THEM (`'$ts_merge'/3`
  and its helpers, the builtins' Prolog half): with no quoted(_) in the
  list, swipl's '$merge_options'/3 is put_dict/3 of `_{quoted:true}` over
  the list, so each option is a key and a value -- `K=V`, `K-V`, `K:V` or
  `K(V)`, anything else type_error('key-value', E) -- its key an atom or
  an integer (else type_error('dict-key', K), an unbound one
  instantiation_error) and given once (else duplicate_key(K)), each named
  put_dict/3; the merge's quoted(true) wins over the list's `quoted =
  false`; and an integer key reaches the write as format/3's
  type_error(atom, K). Through 3.46.0 the list went to the write as it
  was. A list that holds quoted(_) goes as it is, as swipl's.
- A WRITE OPTION SAID TWICE IS ITS LAST (`coco_wt_put`,
  lib/builtins-format.cicili, swipl's scan_options()):
  `write_term('A', [quoted(true), quoted(false)])` writes `A`, and the
  second variable_names/1 names the variables. Through 3.46.0 a boolean
  was on if any of its options said true (quoted, ignore_ops, numbervars),
  and the first variable_names/1 named them -- which also hid the merge's
  quoted(true) above: the first arms found its rule green, and it is red
  now.
- A READ TAKES `Name = Value` AS THE WRITE DOES (`coco_bi_read_term_from_atom`,
  lib/solve-text.cicili): read_term_from_atom/3 and term_string/3's read
  answer `variable_names = V` and pass `foo = bar` over, the last
  variable_names said the one answered; a name that is no atom is still
  type_error(option, E). Through 3.46.0 every `=` was type_error(option,
  E).

## What user sees of the system's and the libraries' predicates, as swipl's (3.48.0)

The owner's ask: finish predicate_property/2, importing no predicate from
swipl that cocolog does not define. 3.41.0 gave predicate_property/2
swipl 9.0.4's answers for the system's predicates and the carried
libraries' exports, and 3.42.0 gave current_predicate/1 named whole its
view of them. A scan of every predicate the two define, each asked of
both in a fresh process, still differed where swipl's user sees what is
neither -- the list's own predicate, the hooks swipl declares in user,
four predicates its autoloader brings from libraries cocolog does not
carry -- and where it sees nothing at all: a carried library's own
predicates, and the exports no autoloading reaches. It agrees now but for
what COMPAT.md says (a predicate the two write differently, the counts of
the clauses each holds, a library's file); what only cocolog defines --
library(async), the store, call_limited/3 -- answers what it did.

- THE LIST'S PREDICATE IS SWIPL'S `'[|]'/2` (`coco-emit-swipl-props`,
  lib/builtins.cicili): cocolog's list functor is '.'/2 (COMPAT.md) and the
  table's row is `'[|]'/2`'s, so the lookup asks '.'/2 as it.
  `predicate_property([_|_], P)` answers built_in, imported_from(system),
  transparent, `(meta_predicate[:|+])` and nodebug, as swipl's, where
  3.47.0 answered `[interpreted,visible,static,nodebug,...]`. Its clauses
  are swipl's two (lib/library.cicili), `[X] :- !, consult(X).` and `[M:F|R]
  :- consult(M:[F|R]).`, under `:- meta_predicate([:|+])`, where 3.47.0's
  were over `'$lf_load'/2`: so `[user:a, b]` is consult/1 of `user:[a,
  b]`, and clause/2 and listing/1 show what swipl's show.
- META_PREDICATE/1 OF A LIST DECLARES THE LIST'S PREDICATE
  (`coco_pred_meta_note`, lib/kb-pred.cicili), as swipl's meta_declaration()
  reads a list and as `coco_pred_meta_check` walks it: through 3.47.0 the
  note took the list's elements for heads, and `[:|+]` declared (:)/0 and
  (+)/0. `meta_predicate([m(0)])` stays swipl's
  type_error(meta_argument_specifier, m(0)).
- CONSULT/1 OF M:F READS F (`'$lf_load'/2`): one namespace, so the module
  a file is loaded into is passed by -- `consult(user:a)`,
  `load_files(user:a, [])` and the list's `consult(user:[a, b])` -- where
  3.47.0 raised existence_error(source_sink, user:a).
- THE FOUR PREDICATES SWIPL'S AUTOLOADER BRINGS FROM A LIBRARY COCOLOG
  DOES NOT CARRY are rows of their libraries (`also/1` in
  tools/props/tables.pl): random/1 (library(random)), make_directory_path/1
  (files_ex), string_to_atom/2 and sumlist/2 (backward_compatibility), each
  of which cocolog defines. imported_from(M) is swipl's module, and
  current_predicate/1 is false until predicate_property/2 named the head,
  as swipl's autoload makes it user's, and true after. Through 3.47.0
  imported_from answered nothing, string_to_atom/2 was current from the
  start and the other three never.
- WHAT USER DOES NOT SEE IS NO PREDICATE OF USER'S (`coco_pp_unseen`,
  lib/builtins-db.cicili; flags 4096 and 8192 of lib/swipl-props.cicili).
  The generator rows each predicate a carried library's file defines that
  swipl's user does not see, flag 4096: 291 of them, a library's helper
  (assoc's gen_assoc_/3, aggregate's add_existential_vars/3, ugraphs'
  before/2) and what a library defines in another module
  (error:has_type/2, sandbox:safe_meta_predicate/1,
  prolog_colour:goal_colours/2, prolog:called_by/4). predicate_property/2
  answers no property of one but implementation_module(user), and
  current_predicate/1 is false, as swipl's; through 3.47.0 each was the
  store's predicate, the module of the library that defined it: has_type/2
  the 38 clauses library(error) and library(assoc) give it,
  imported_from(assoc), and the three hooks library(yall) defines for
  sandbox, prolog_colour and prolog imported_from(yall).
  Flag 8192 marks the 29 exports of library(dcg/basics) and
  library(dcg/high_order), which swipl's autoloader does not reach:
  digits//1, string_without//2, sequence//2, optional//2 and the rest are no
  predicates of user's until the program loads their library
  (`coco_imp_has`), and swipl's properties after; predicate_property/2 of
  one no longer imports it (`'$pp_autoload'/1`). Through 3.47.0 the two
  libraries, read at every start, were user's from the start, each export
  current and its library's module its implementation_module. Neither flag
  answers where the program gave the name a clause of its own
  (`coco_pred_prog_clause`, `muted` 0): a clause consulted or asserted
  makes the predicate user's own, as a definition in user is in swipl,
  however the library's clauses beside it in the one namespace (card row
  N1) -- `before(uv, x).` is `[interpreted,visible,static,defined]` and
  current (`coco_pred_current`, lib/kb.cicili, the same rule), where
  ugraphs' before/2 is hidden; through 3.47.0 it was not current.
- THE HOOKS SWIPL DECLARES IN USER ARE ROWS OF USER'S (17, the generator's
  user clause of `pred/2`): term_expansion/2,4, goal_expansion/2,4,
  message_hook/3, library_directory/1, file_search_path/2,
  prolog_file_type/2, portray/1, prolog_load_file/2, resource/2,3,
  expand_query/4 and expand_answer/2 dynamic and multifile, exception/3
  notrace too, message_property/2 and prolog_list_goal/1 multifile --
  answered from the row, so file_search_path/2 is no nodebug predicate
  though the files half reads it under generate_debug_info false, and
  current_predicate/1 is true of each the store holds
  (`coco_b_cp_current`'s `user`). The hooks cocolog's libraries ask are
  declared where they are asked, dynamic and multifile: term_expansion/2
  (lib/dcg.cicili), message_hook/3 (library/print_message.pl),
  library_directory/1, file_search_path/2 and prolog_file_type/2
  (lib/files.cicili) -- current from the start, a program's clauses join
  them, and an assert or a retract changes them. Through 3.47.0
  term_expansion/2 and message_hook/3 were no predicates before a clause of
  the program's, goal_expansion/2 not current, library_directory/1 not
  multifile, and file_search_path/2 and prolog_file_type/2 static, nodebug
  and not current. listing/0 writes the three with no clause of the
  libraries' (`:- dynamic library_directory/1.` and its `:- multifile`,
  message_hook/3's and term_expansion/2's), as swipl's writes its hooks
  (test/repl.pl). A hook cocolog asks of no program (portray/1,
  exception/3, ...) is no predicate before a clause of the program's
  (COMPAT.md).
