## listing/1's meta_predicate lines, and transparency as the spec says (3.48.2)

listing/1 wrote no `:- meta_predicate` declaration through 3.48.1: a
listing of a meta-predicate, read back, lost what made it one. It writes
swipl 9.0.4's library(listing) declarations now (`coco_listing_pred` in
lib/solve-db.cicili): after the thread_local, dynamic, volatile, multifile
and public lines, the spec predicate_property/2 answers
(`coco_meta_spec_term`, moved there from lib/builtins-db.cicili), with the
predicate's module before it where the listing is not that module's
(`:- meta_predicate lmq:lmq_p(0).` from user, `lmq_p(0)` from lmq), then a
module_transparent line unless the spec names a module (an argument 0 to
9, `:`, `^` or `//`: swipl's meta_implies_transparent/1), and the blank
line after a declaration that stands alone. A predicate a
meta_predicate/1 or a module_transparent/1 alone declared is none to
listing/1, as swipl's (existence_error).

The spec is kept as swipl's meta_declaration() keeps it
(`coco_pred_meta_note` in lib/kb-pred.cicili): `*` is `?`
(`meta_predicate mq2(+,-,?)`, where 3.48.1 answered `*`), and the
predicate is transparent as its spec says, a module_transparent/1 before
the spec taken away, one after it standing (through 3.48.1 kept, so
`:- module_transparent b2/1. :- meta_predicate b2(?).` was transparent,
which swipl's is not). Every reader of transparency asks the spec as
predicate_property/2's transparent did (`coco_meta_spec_module`, moved to
lib/kb-pred.cicili): a last call under `$/0` drops its guard into a
predicate whose spec names a module (`coco_det_transparent`, as swipl's
I_DEPART: through 3.48.1 `meta_predicate dg_p(0)` carried the guard into
dg_p and `g_p :- $, dg_p(member(_, [1, 2])).` raised
determinism_error(dg_p/1, det, nondet, guard_in_caller), where swipl's
succeeds); and such a predicate's clauses make their meta calls in its own
module, a module_transparent/1 after the spec notwithstanding
(`coco_meta_ctx`, as swipl's frame keeps its definition's module: through
3.48.1 the caller's, user's, which a predicate module_transparent/1 alone
made transparent still takes). The first cut, which took the earlier
module_transparent/1 away and asked the bit alone, carried the guard into
`:- module_transparent dg_b/1. :- meta_predicate dg_b(0).`, which 3.48.1
dropped: found by a probe of each reader of the bit (`pattrs` 4) against
swipl before the case was done.

## A body's `X = X` stored as `true`, as swipl's compiler keeps it (3.48.3)

swipl's compileBodyUnify() makes a unification of a variable with itself
I_TRUE, and its clause/2 and listing/1 give it back as `true`; cocolog kept
it as written (`p(X) :- X = X` was `p(A) :- A=A`). Found by 3.48.2's
listing case, where `mq(G, X, M) :- call(G, X), M = M.` lists swipl's
`call(A, B), true`. It is `true` now wherever the body runs it
(`coco_cbody_void` in lib/kb-consult.cicili, asked before the clause's
variables are counted): in a conjunction, in the arms of `;`, `->`, `*->`
and `\+`, under a qualifier, a variable one too, and in `$/1` and `@/2`.
In a goal's argument it is data, and stays (`call(X = X)`,
`forall(X = X, true)`), as two terms stay (`f(X) = f(X)`).

The unifications that begin the body move into the head past it, as
swipl's do: `p(X) :- X = X, X = a.` is `p(a) :- true`, a file's or a
first assert's, and `p(X, Y) :- X = X, Y = b.` is `p(A, b) :- true`.
cocolog moves only a variable the clause names nowhere else, and an
`X = X` the body runs now names it nowhere: the move's count leaves such
goals out (`coco_cbody_selfeq`, walking the constructs as
`coco_cbody_goal` does). The void rule keeps its count, as swipl's void
variables are counted over the whole clause: `p :- X = X, X = f(Y),
b(Y)` keeps `A=f(B)`. A `:- dynamic` predicate's clause moves nothing, as
before (`sd(X) :- X = X, X = a` is `sd(A) :- true, A=a`).

| D04 | ... the arms of `;`, `\|`, `->` and `*->` |
| D05 | ... `\+`, `$/1` and `@/2` |
| D06 | ... a qualifier, a variable one too |

## write_term/2's max_depth(D), as swipl's pl-write.c applies it (3.49.0)

write_term/2, write_term/3 and format's `~W` checked `max_depth(D)` and
read it past: every term was written whole. A minor, as what a program
writes moves.

- A term past D is `...` (swipl's writeTerm(), `++depth > max_depth`).
  The term written is at depth 1 and each argument one deeper -- a
  compound's, an operator's operands, a curly term's -- so `f(g(h))` at 2
  is `f(g(...))` and `1+2+3` at 1 `... + ...`.
- A list's elements go one deeper each (swipl's writeList()): the K-th of
  a list at depth L is at L + K, a list that would go past D ends
  `|...]`, and an improper tail is one deeper than the element before it.
  `[1,2,3,4]` at 3 is `[1,2|...]`.
- `...` takes the spaces an atom of symbol characters would, as swipl's
  needSpace() gives them: `... + ...`, `- ...`, `a: ... : ...`,
  `x is ... + ...`, and none beside a letter, `...mod...`, `dynamic...`.
- D of 0 is no limit, a negative D elides the term itself, and the last
  max_depth/1 of the options counts. D past an int is
  representation_error(int), and so is priority(P), as swipl's OPT_INT;
  through 3.48.3 any integer was taken for either.
- A cyclic term under a limit is written to it, `f(f(f(f(...))))`, where
  with none it is written as its factors. Past 1 024 the writer's cycle
  guard meets it first (COMPAT.md).

The limit is the machine's `wmax` and the write's mode bit 1024, both set
by `coco_wt_put` around one write. `coco_write_rec` tests the bit first
and reads `wmax` only under it, and a list under it is
`coco_write_list_cut`'s, out of line. A compound and a list hand on
`mode & 2011`, where they handed on `mode & 987`.

test/files/write_depth.pl, new, holds 438 lines to swipl, byte for byte
(3.48.3 differs at the 42nd).

The arms, one build each over the writer's four cases (write_depth,
write, print, escapes): the arm of no edit green in all four, and each of
the ten rules red in write_depth -- a term past the limit `...`, a list
under a limit the cut writer's, its `|...]`, its K-th element K deeper
than the list, a compound's children carrying the limit, the option read,
D of 0 no limit, the option's range, an improper tail one deeper than
the element before it, and spacing(next_argument) in a cut list. Each is
green in the other three but D of 0, which is red in write and escapes
too: with the bit set for every write, each write_term/2 writes `...`.

The cost where no limit is set is one instruction a term written. A run
that writes a term of 2 019 subterms ninety times (write/1, writeq/1 and
print/1, 181 710 terms) counts `coco_write_rec` 184 884 instructions
more, +0.10 % of its 177.5 million. tools/flow/zero.sh against 3.48.3,
the binaries at like paths, work less padding: nrev +11 instructions,
queens +0, lookup +0. A start (`cocolog query true`, each binary at the
checkout's path) counts 14 693 more of 35 745 106, the writer's own 47
of them and the rest libc's memcmp and strcmp, which move with a
binary's layout.

## An -s script's and a module's goal_expansion/2, asked of them (3.49.1)

`cocolog -s FILE` did not ask FILE's own goal_expansion/2 of FILE's
clauses, where `swipl FILE` does, and a file read as a module did not ask
its own of its clauses either. library(yall)'s clause of goal_expansion/2
(swipl's `system:goal_expansion/2`, its lambda compiler) is read at
start-up into the one namespace, so the predicate's first clause was a
library's; a module's read gave it a muted clause after that, and a muted
clause counted as a hook only where the predicate's first clause was a
program file's (`own`). So `t :- foo(1).` after `goal_expansion(foo(X),
bar(X)).` in a script called foo/1, an unknown procedure, where swipl calls
bar/1. A consulted file's hook counted, unmuted, and term_expansion/2
counted any live clause, so `cocolog run` of a file with its hook in it was
right, and a module read after a consulted hook met it.

- A clause of goal_expansion/2 counts as a hook unless a library's own
  text gave it: a read under `noexp` (a compiled-in module's text, a
  preloaded library's) that stores one notes its origin on the store
  (`xlib`, in `coco_assert_from`), and `coco_xhook_bits` passes over a
  muted clause of such an origin. yall's clause stays no hook: counted,
  every load after it would ask goal_expansion/2 of every goal.
- A module's own hook is asked of its clauses, as swipl's. One
  namespace's, it is asked of every file read after it too, where swipl
  asks it of that module's clauses alone (COMPAT.md).

a module whose own hook rewrites its clauses, read before the program has

and term_expansion/2 asked of it, and a script with no hook asking none

The arms, one build each over expand_module, expand and script: the clause

## sort/4's key paths and order names, and atomics_to_string/3's split (3.50.0)

sort/4 took an integer or an atom for its key and only @< @=< @> @>= for
its order, and atomics_to_string/3 raised instantiation_error for an
unbound list. A minor, as calls that raised now sort and split.

- A PROPER LIST OF KEYS IS A PATH, swipl's sort/4 (pl-list.c,
  get_key_arg_ex()): `sort([1, 2], @<, L, S)` sorts each `f(g(_, K))` by
  K, each step a positive integer or an atom (a dict key, `[]` among them,
  an atom to swipl's C). 0 or a negative step is
  domain_error(not_less_than_one, K); a step of any other kind -- a
  string, a float, a compound, a list, an unbound one -- fails with no
  error, as swipl's returns FALSE. Through 3.49.1 a list was
  type_error(sort_key, L).
- Each element is walked step by step, swipl's extract_key():
  type_error(compound, T), then type_error(dict, T) for an atom's step,
  then existence_error(argument, K, T), T the term the walk has reached.
- A positive key past swipl 9.0.4's tagged integers, 2^56 - 1 (its
  max_tagged_integer on 64 bits), fails, at the top or as a step, as
  swipl's FALSE there.
- The order is read after the whole key as PL_get_atom_ex() reads it:
  anything but an atom type_error(atom, O), where through 3.49.1 it was
  domain_error(order, O); and swipl's other names, `<`, `=<`, `>` and
  `>=`, sort as `@<`, `@=<`, `@>` and `@>=`, where each was that
  domain error too.
- atomics_to_string/3 splits an unbound tail as atomic_list_concat/3
  does, swipl's one atomic_list_concat() for PL_STRING: the text of the
  third argument cut at the separator, the parts ATOMS as split_atom()
  makes them, and an empty separator domain_error(non_empty_atom, Sep).
  An unbound element is instantiation_error still, as swipl's: only the
  atom's version splits there. The split is the engine's now
  (`coco_tx_split`, lib/solve-text.cicili), which atomic_list_concat/3
  shares; library(flow)'s table has the new mode and the two text rows.

test/files/sort_keys.pl, new, holds 115 lines to swipl, byte for byte
(3.49.1 differs at 53 of them).

The arms, one build each over sort_keys: the arm of no edit green, and
each of the nine rules red -- a list of keys a path, a step of another
kind a failure, 0 no step, each element walked step by step, the tagged
bound, the order's other names, the order's type_error(atom, O), the
split of an unbound tail and its empty separator.

The cost: a comparison reads its key along the path the walk checked,
with no arity test of its own. Four sorts of 20 000 elements (keysort/2,

## prolog_load_context/2's module, variable_names, term and reloading (3.51.0)

prolog_load_context/2 answered `module` as `user` wherever it was asked,
and `variable_names`, `term` and `reloading` not at all, where swipl
9.0.4's boot/syspred.pl answers each while a load reads. A minor, as the
four answer now.

- `module` is the module/2 read's module while a load reads its file (the
  read's `ssu_mod`), and `user` outside one and where no load reads -- an
  initialization/1 goal run after its file among them, as swipl's
  '$current_source_module' is.
- `variable_names` is the term in hand's bindings, `[Name = Var, ...]` in
  the order the reader met the names (`_` none, `_X` one), while the load
  asks term_expansion/2 or goal_expansion/2 of the term and while a
  directive's goal runs: the term's own variables, bound as the goal binds
  them. `[]` at a file's end and outside a load. At a file's start, and in
  a directive the start expands to, they are those of the read around the
  load -- a nested load's are its directive's -- as swipl's begin_of_file
  sets no '$variable_names'. They are built when a goal asks, from the
  reader's names (`coco_consult_vn`): the machine points at the reader
  (`sloc_rd`), and a directive's goal, which may collect, holds the
  reader's variables as a root of the collector.
- `term` is the term as read while a hook runs (`sloc_tp`): the read term
  still where goal_expansion/2 is asked of a clause term_expansion/2 gave,
  or of a grammar rule's translation. `[]` while a directive's goal runs,
  and failing outside a load, as swipl's '$term' reads.
- `reloading` is true through a read of a file the store read before
  (`coco_consult_oid`'s AGAIN), a nested read's its own, and fails
  otherwise.

What stays apart (COMPAT.md's row): `stream` fails, a load reading text;
and expand_term/2 called as a goal sets no '$term', which swipl's sets to
the term while its hooks run and to `[]` after. That waits on b_setval/2,
which here is nb_setval/2 under another name -- it copies its term and
nothing undoes it -- where swipl's is backtrackable (the next task).

(3.50.0 differs at 94 of them): the case writes the files it loads --
a file with an include, a hook asked of a term with `_X` in it, goal
expansion of a clause, directives with variables, a nested consult from
a directive with a variable, a file read again, a first read that reads
another again, a module and the module read again, the start and the
end of each, a directive the start expands to -- and reports each key at
each place. test/gc.pl's directive section binds a directive's variables
across a collection and prints the bindings after it, in the file run
and as the first directive of a file a directive loads.

The arms, one build each, every rule taken out alone: the arm of no edit
green, and each of the sixteen rules red -- fifteen in load_context, and
the root in test/gc.pl, which holds three of the others to it too. The
rules: `module` the read's (red), `user` where no load reads (red), the
bindings asked at all (red in both), the term while a hook runs (red),
`[]` while a directive's goal runs (red), `reloading` through a read the
store read before (red) and a nested read's flag put back (red), a
directive's term and reader put back after its goal (red), a hook's
(red), a hook's bindings the reader's (red), the bindings around the
load at a file's start (red) and none at its end (red), a directive's
bindings the reader's (red in both), a directive the start expands to
keeping the ones around the load (red), the bindings in the reader's
order (red in both), and the reader's variables a root of the collector

## b_setval/2 and b_getval/2 as swipl's, and expand_term/2's '$term' (3.52.0)

b_setval/2 was nb_setval/2 under another name: it copied its term into
the store and nothing undid it, where swipl 9.0.4's (pl-gvar.c) links the
term itself and trails the assignment, so backtracking puts back what the
key held before. A minor, as the global now answers what it did not.

- **The box.** A key b_setval/2 names gets an entry in the machine's table
  (`gvb`, never removed), and each b_setval/2 a BOX on the heap,
  `'$gv'(Serial, Value)`, made with its value cell a reference to itself
  -- the dead mark -- and the value written into it as setarg/3 writes
  (`coco_trail_pair`), so backtracking past the write puts the old word
  back and backtracking past the making puts the dead mark back. A box is
  live while its header, its serial and a value cell that is no dead mark
  stand where it was put, inside the heap (`coco-gvb-live`): a freeze that
  keeps the heap (nb_setarg/3 into an older term) still loses the box to
  the trail, and a box a collection kept past its choice point -- its
  trail entry dropped there, as a newer cell's is -- is past the heap
  backtracking leaves. The value is the term itself: a binding made after
  it is seen, setarg/3 on it writes the global.
- **Reads.** nb_getval/2, b_getval/2 and nb_current/2 read a live box
  first and the store's global after; nb_current/2 with its key unbound
  names the boxes' keys the store lacks. nb_setval/2 takes the key from
  its box, so a b_setval/2 undone after it brings nothing back.
- **The collector** marks every live box as a root, forgets a dead one,
  and moves each box with its cells.
- **A load's goal ends what it did, as swipl's failure-driven load loop
  fails back over each term it reads.** A directive's and an
  initialization goal's work is undone when it succeeds too (`\+ \+ G`:
  `lb_goal_hook` undoes its trail), a box made since the goal began is
  dead (its serial past the goal's clock: a collection in the goal drops
  the trail entry that made a box newer than its barrier, so no undo puts
  its dead mark back), and an expansion hook keeps its output and its
  bindings of the term in hand while what it did to a cell older than the
  term -- a b_setval/2 into a box made before the load, a binding or a
  setarg/3 of a term in one -- is undone as it returns (`coco_undo_older`,
  below the term's floor `lfloor`, the consult's mark for the term, set as
  each term begins and put back around a nested read). A copy of a ground
  global the goal read stays, and so does its sentinel (`coco_undo_older`'s
  KEEP): the consult's mark was raised over the copy at the fill. A
  directive an expansion gave binds nothing the next term it gave sees
  (`o_done(_)`, swipl's).
- **expand_term/2 sets '$term'**, the term while its hooks run and `[]`
  after (lib/dcg.cicili, swipl's expand_term/4), and prolog_load_context/2's
  `term` reads its box where it was written in the goal in hand, else the
  load's term: a load's own hooks see the load's term whatever an
  expand_term/2 before the load left set. COMPAT.md's row 39 keeps
  `stream` alone.

THE FIRST CUT'S HOLE, found by a probe written for the COMPAT row it was
going to need: a directive's b_setval/2 into a box made before the load
wrote a value from the directive's own heap, which the consult winds back
after the term, so the next directive read it as cells of whatever the
load read next (`@(S_1,[S_1=next_directive((print(S_1),nl))])`), and a
hook's binding of a variable in such a box the same (`f(end_of_file)`).
swipl undoes both as the term ends; cocolog does now, at the goal's end.
What stays apart (COMPAT.md, a new row): a hook's b_setval/2 -- to a key
of its own (`hz-1` in swipl, `hz-unset` here) or into an older box -- and
its work on a term in one are undone as the hook returns, where swipl's
stand until every term its expansion gave is done, so a directive the
hook's own expansion gave does not see them (`o6-y` in swipl, `o6-1`
here). The faithful form is a barrier the collector knows at each term's
start, as swipl's failure-driven loop has a choice point there, and its
undo at every way the term's processing ends: a lead.

THE SECOND CUT'S HOLE, found by a count: the undo at a directive's end took
the sentinel of each ground global's copy the directive read with the rest
of its work, so every directive that read one copied it again -- a load of
500 directives each reading a list of 2 000 counted 105 075 129
instructions where 3.51.0 counts 49 939 240, and kept a copy a directive
until a collection. The sentinels are kept now, from the goal's trail mark
in their order, each copy told where its own stands (49 987 594, +0.10 %).
test/engine.pl's `gvars_runs` holds it: 100 directives over a list of 600
grow the heap by no copy.

The arms, one build each, every rule taken out alone, each over
global_vars.pl and test/engine.pl's `gvars_runs`: the arm of no edit green
in both, and each of the thirty rules red. Twelve are red in both cases --
the write as setarg/3 writes, its old value kept and the trail's value
entry; a box live while its value is no dead mark, and made with one; its
serial; nb_getval/2's and b_getval/2's read of the box first; the
collector's mark of each live box and its move of the box's place; a
goal's undo at its end; what a hook did to what is older than its term
undone as it returns; the term's floor set as it begins; an older cell's
value entry put back and an older variable unbound. Eleven in
global_vars.pl alone -- nb_setval/2 taking the key from its box;
nb_current/2's read of the box and the keys it names; a box made in a goal
a load ran ended with it; the clock where that goal began, which a '$term'
written before it is none of, and the clock of the goal around it put
back; prolog_load_context/2's `term` reading '$term' where this goal wrote
it; expand_term/2 setting it, and the machine knowing its entry; a hook's
goal saying it is one. And two in `gvars_runs` alone: the box's bounds,
where t(40)'s box stands past the heap under trace and under the
collector, and a directive keeping its copies' sentinels, which the probe
of the copies counts.

Five were green over the first cut of the cases, and the cases were
sharpened until each went red: the box's header (`coco-gvb-live`), which
the serial and the value cover wherever a term built over a dead box
leaves them unlike the box's -- `first_box` now builds f/30 where main's
first box stood, each argument the box's serial, 2, and `gvars_runs` the
same in a file of its own, serial 1 (`unset` in swipl; the box's value
without the header); the hook's flag cleared as a goal begins, so that a
load the hook runs has directives of its own -- which matters only where
no hook of that load clears it first, as each term's own ask of the hooks
does before the term's goal runs, so the case's last hook takes every hook
away (`retractall/1`, as swipl's dynamic hooks allow) and then consults a
file whose second directive reads what its first wrote into a box made
before the load (`nr1-1`; without the clear, `nr1-nr`, and the directive
after the load read from heap the consult gave back); and the term's floor
put back after a nested read and after an include, so that a term an
expansion gives after a directive that consults a file, or includes one,
keeps the bindings its goal expansion made (`n4-bound`, `n5-bound`): left
where the nested read set it, the floor stood above the given term and
undid them; and the copy told where its sentinel stands once the undo has
moved it -- each of the copies' directives binds a variable of its own
before it reads, the one that copies the global among them, so the
sentinel goes down over the binding's entry, where the first cut's stood
first on the trail and never moved (without it every directive copies the
global again, 1 932 664 cells). Through the first cut the probe of the
header (`f(1, z, _)` by arg/3) bound each argument to a cell of its goal
and built nothing over the box.

cocolint's card row G1 is retired with its S1 pattern (b_setval/2 "IS
nb_setval": 25 rows, 37 cites, six patterns); lesson basics/12 teaches the
backtrackable global, lesson library/37 counts the card again, and
test/lint.pl's acknowledgements are X3's and P1's.

test/files/global_vars.pl, new, holds 106 lines to swipl, byte for byte:
the box's write, link, binding, setarg/3, undo by backtracking, a throw,

over a box and under one, a term built over a dead box; a directive of its

The cost, against 3.51.0 at like paths: a start counts 35 788 692

5 000 clauses and 500 directives, no hook: +103 140 (+0.06 %), of which
coco_undo_older is 18 000 and lb_goal_hook +9 000 (the directive's undo,
36 and 18 instructions a directive), and libc's memcmp +47 049 and strcmp

## write_term/2's fullstop(B), nl(B), dotlists(B) and no_lists(B), as swipl's (3.53.0)

write_term/2, write_term/3 and format's `~W` took the four options and wrote
as if none had been given: a term under fullstop(true) ended with no full
stop, a list under dotlists(true) came out a list. swipl 9.0.4's pl-write.c
writes each of them, and so does cocolog now. A minor, as what a program
writes moves.

- **fullstop(true)** ends the term with `.`, a space before it where the
  term's last token and the stop would read as one (`- .`, `:- .`, `\ .`,
  `# .`, `1- - 1.` stays as it is), then a space, or with nl(true) a
  newline; **nl(true)** alone ends it with a newline (swipl's
  `PutToken(".")`, then `nl ? '\n' : ' '`). The last of each in the list
  counts, and `fullstop` with no argument is `fullstop(true)`, as an
  option list says. `coco_write_fullstop` asks `coco_needs_gap` of the
  last byte written and the stop, the test each token's space comes from.
- **dotlists(true)** writes a list as the compounds it is, `.(H,T)`, the
  `.` a token of its own (`- .(1,[])`, `a- .(1,[])`), and **no_lists(true)**
  as `'[|]'(H,T)`, the atom swipl names its cells by, quoted as a quoted
  write quotes it (`[|](1,[])` unquoted). dotlists(true) wins where both are
  given. Under max_depth(D) each element is one deeper than the one before,
  as the list's own walk counts them, and a tail past the limit is `...`
  (`.(1,.(2,...))`); spacing(next_argument) puts its space after each
  comma; a tail that is no list is written as itself (`.(a,b)`); and a
  tail that comes back on itself is found as the list's walk finds it
  (Brent's), the write taken back and the term's factors written. The
  list's end and a list inside an argument or a curly term are written so
  too, a string under `codes` among them (`.(97,.(98,[]))`), and `[](x)` is
  no list. `coco_write_list` asks one test of the two bits and the depth
  limit's (`mode & 7168`), where it asked one of the limit's alone, and
  the cut writer, out of line, hands a list under 2048 or 4096 on to
  `coco_write_list_dots`, out of line and weak; a compound and a list hand
  the two bits on (`mode & 8155`, where they handed on `mode & 2011`).
- **A boolean option is true, false, on, off, 1 or 0** (swipl's OPT_BOOL),
  every one write_term/2 takes: `quoted(1)` quotes, `quoted(2)` is
  type_error(bool, 2), as swipl's; through 3.52.0 the integers were
  type errors too.

test/files/write_options.pl, new, holds 100 lines to swipl, byte for byte
(3.52.0 differs at 84 of them). test/cyclic.pl's long and deep section
writes a list of 3 000 that is its own tail under each of the two.

The arms, one build each, every rule taken out alone, each over
write_options.pl and test/cyclic.pl: the arm of no edit green in both, and
each of the fifteen rules red. Six are red in both -- dotlists(true) and
no_lists(true) asked for, the two bits carried down to the arguments, a
tail that is no list written as itself, the list writer's one test and the
cut writer's hand-on; eight in write_options.pl alone -- the integer
booleans, the full stop, its gap and its newline, nl(true) alone, dotlists
the stronger, a tail past the limit and next_argument's space; and one in
cyclic.pl alone, the tail that comes back on itself.

The cost is none where neither option is asked. A run that writes 36 540
lists (a term of 406, ninety times by write/1, writeq/1 and print/1)
counts `coco_write_list` the same to the instruction as 3.52.0, the run
+24 000 of 101.7 million (+0.024 %), all of it libc's strcmp and memcmp
and the loader at the strings' new addresses. The first cut asked a test
of its own for the two bits ahead of the depth limit's: the list writer
kept its mode on the stack for it, a padding no-op stood after the test,
and each list written cost nine instructions more (+327 690, +0.32 % of
the run). tools/flow/zero.sh against 3.52.0 at like paths, work less
padding: nrev +11 instructions, queens +0, lookup +0.

Narrow cases green: lint, files, syntax, cyclic, string, units, errors,
repl, trace, backtrace, directives, engine, library, journal, reconsult,
window, flowdebug and flowchart. Reasoning stays 1.0.27.

## print/1's portray/1, and write_term/2's portray(true) and portray_goal(G), as swipl's (3.54.0)

print/1, format's `~p` and write_term/2's portray(true) and portray_goal(G)
wrote as writeq/1 writes and called nothing: the hook and the write's goal
were read past. swipl 9.0.4's pl-write.c asks each, and so does cocolog
now. A minor, as what a program writes moves.

- **portray/1 is asked of each term but a variable**, the term first, then
  its arguments, a list's elements, a tail that is no list, an operator's
  operands, a curly term's argument, a number, a string -- and the list's
  end only where it is no list's end (`h([])`, `[[]]`). The depth limit is
  asked before it: a term past max_depth(D) is `...`, whatever a goal
  would have written. It is asked where the program has a clause for it,
  as swipl asks it only then, so a print/1 of a program with none writes
  as it wrote (`coco_portray_defined`, portray/1's name interned once a
  machine). **portray_goal(G)** is `call(G, T, Opts)`, Opts the write's own
  options with every priority(_) dropped and the term's priority(P) last;
  portray(true) and portray_goal(G) imply numbervars(true) unless the
  options say.
- **The goal is a search of its own**, its output captured and put on the
  write's text (`coco_portray_call` over `coco_out_capture_run`): run
  untraced, as swipl's PL_Q_NODEBUG runs it, its bindings undone and its
  other work kept, the writer's state of the machine saved around it, its
  cells given back, and no deeper than 100 goals (swipl's
  MAX_PORTRAY_NESTING: past it, resource_error(portray_nesting) in the
  innermost write's context, system:print/1, system:format/2 or
  system:write_term/2).
- **No gap goes before a goal's text**, as each of swipl's writes starts
  afresh with no last character (`1+-1`, `--1`, `dynamicxx`), and the
  spaces swipl writes whatever follows stay: a space before an infix
  operator is one after it too, and next_argument's after a comma. A goal
  that fails having written leaves its text and the term after it, a
  space between where the two would read as one token (`partial w`).
- **A goal that throws stops the write**: what came before stays, the
  goal's own text too, and nothing more is written; what a parent wrote
  after the stop is taken back, each operand written into a buffer of its
  own carrying the stop up as it is put on its parent's
  (`coco_write_cut_up`). The builtin raises the ball once its text is out,
  and fullstop(true) and nl(true) write nothing after it (swipl 9.0.4's
  write_term/2 says there that its foreign predicate did not clear the
  exception, and the catch around it binds nothing: COMPAT.md).
- **A cyclic term is written in its factors from the first**, as swipl asks
  PL_is_acyclic() before it writes, so no goal is asked of the term
  unwound (unless a depth limit is set, as for any write).
- **portray/1 is declared in user, dynamic and multifile, as swipl's**
  (the builtins half, as the grammar half declares term_expansion/2,
  3.48.0): current from the start, predicate_property/2 answers both,
  listing/0 writes its two declarations, and a call of it with no clause
  fails, where through 3.53.0 it was an unknown procedure.
- **The tracer writes a goal as print/1 does** (swipl's debugger writes a
  frame's goal with `~p`): `print(f(zz))` where portray/1 writes `zz`. A
  goal that throws there cuts the line where it threw, as swipl's does,
  and its ball is given back unraised, where swipl's goes up into the
  program at a later port (COMPAT.md).

The compound writer is one body, `coco-write-fun-body`, emitted twice:
the plain copy, 3.53.0's code but for its mask, which no write that asks
nothing leaves, and the copy for a write that asks portray
(`coco_write_fun_p`), whose operators keep the goal's first text and carry
the stop up.

test/files/portray.pl, new, holds 192 lines to swipl, byte for byte; 3.53.0
differs at 170 of them. test/trace.pl's `pq` holds the tracer's text and the
untraced goal to swipl, and two lines of its own the goal that throws as a
port is written; test/errors.pl's `portray_stops` the write a goal stopped
under fullstop(true); test/files/user_view.pl the declaration, and
test/repl.pl listing/0's two lines of it.

The arms, one build each, every rule taken out alone, each over
portray.pl, print.pl, test/trace.pl and test/errors.pl's `portray_stops`
(the declaration's over user_view.pl and test/repl.pl): the arm of no edit
green in all four, and twenty-nine of the thirty-two rules red. In
portray.pl alone: the gap before a goal's text after an infix operator
and after a prefix one, the stop carried up from an infix's right operand
and from a prefix's operand, a failed goal's text kept and the gap after
it, a cyclic term written in its factors first, the depth limit first, a
term asked once, a list's elements carried down, numbervars(true) implied,
portray_goal's priorities dropped and its own last, the nesting limit,
print/1's hook, the ball `~p` and `~W` raise, a stopped write asking no
more, a goal's first text noted, the outer write's state put back and a
goal's bindings undone; in test/trace.pl alone the goal run untraced, the
tracer's text and its ball given back; in `portray_stops` alone the full
stop a stopped write writes none of; in three of the four the hook asked,
the arguments carried down and what a parent wrote after the stop taken
back; and the declaration in user_view.pl and test/repl.pl. Five rules had
no case until one was written for each: the prefix's stop (t(135) to
t(140), bracketed operands), the cyclic term (t(141) and t(142): unwound,
1 025 goals are asked of z where swipl asks one -- the writer walks a
term's first argument down first, so t(132)'s `f(X, z)` asks no z on its
way to the cycle), `~W`'s ball (t(133), t(134)), a stopped write (t(144)
to t(147): a z after the throw is seen) and the bindings (t(148) to
t(150)). Three stay green, as they can: whether portray/1 has a clause
(P24) and a goal's cells given back (P25), guards of cost -- without the

without the second they leave 685 704 cells on the heap where 5 064
stand, 16 a goal -- and the find's bounds check (P23), which no write
reaches since portray/1 is declared in every store, a thread's and
run_isolated/2's too.

The cost is none where no portray/1 clause exists and no portray_goal(G)
is given. tools/flow/zero.sh against 3.53.0 at like paths, work less
padding: nrev +1 instruction, queens +8, lookup +3 977 -- all of lookup's
libc's memset and strncmp at the buffers' new addresses but 18, the
engine's own (`cc_regs_worth`). 3.53.0's write-heavy run (a term of 406,
ninety times by write/1, writeq/1 and print/1) makes the same 127 632
writer calls and counts 631 946 fewer instructions (-0.62 %): libc's
strcmp 629 402 fewer at the names' new addresses, the writer 25 374 fewer,
and each print/1 105 more -- it asks whether portray/1 has a clause. A
start counts 45 552 more of 35.8 million (+0.13 %): the two declarations
read and run, some 12 000, and strcmp 32 768 more, 265 calls of it theirs
and the rest each call's cost at the names' new addresses.

A goal asked costs about 12 500 instructions and eight system calls,
because it runs as a search of its own with its output captured (a file
made, the output's descriptor moved onto it and back, the text read back),
where swipl calls the hook in place: 30 print/1s of a term whose writes

million instructions where 58.7 million write them with no clause, 0.20 s
where swipl takes 0.016 s. Making that cheaper is a task of its own.

Narrow cases green: lint, files, syntax, cyclic, string, units, errors,

window, flowdebug and flowchart. Reasoning stays 1.0.27.

## write_term/2's character_escapes, character_escapes_unicode, quote_non_ascii, brace_terms, cycles and portrayed, as swipl's (3.55.0)

Six of write_term/2's options were checked and read past: a quoted write
under character_escapes(false) still escaped what it wrote,
character_escapes_unicode(false) still wrote `\u0001`, quote_non_ascii(true)
left a name past U+00FF bare, brace_terms(false) wrote `{a}`, cycles(false)
wrote a cyclic term in its factors, and portrayed(true) asked no portray/1.
swipl 9.0.4's pl-write.c applies each, and so does cocolog now; with them a
cycle's factors are named where swipl names them, term_to_atom/2's quoted
text is swipl's, and a failed portray goal leaves no gap before a goal's
text. A minor, as what a program writes moves.

- **character_escapes(false)** writes the quoted text as it is, its quote
  doubled and its backslash `\\` (`'a<LF>b'`, `'it''s'`, `"say ""hi"""`):
  the mode's 256 without 16, swipl's PL_WRT_QUOTED alone. A string's quote
  is doubled there as an atom's is; through 3.54.0 a string kept `\"`.
- **character_escapes_unicode(false)** escapes a character by its code,
  `\x1\` (no 64), where the default is `\u0001`.
- **quote_non_ascii(true)** quotes a name that holds a character past
  U+00FF (`'∀'`, `'αβ'`; never `é`), the mode's 32768, which a compound and
  a list hand down (`mode & 49115`) and an atom reads (`mode & 33105`).
- **brace_terms(false)** writes a curly term `{}(T)`, the mode's 128 that
  write_canonical/1 sets. A compound named `{}` of other arities is
  quoted, `'{}'(a,b)`, only in the engine's own text, where neither 16
  nor 256 is set; every quoted write a program asks for writes it bare.
- **cycles(false)** raises domain_error(cyclic_term, T) of a cyclic term
  before a character is written, whatever the depth limit, as swipl asks
  PL_is_acyclic() once its options are read (`coco_wt_check`); write_term/3
  raises the stream's errors before it (library(stream)'s
  `stream_wt_err`).
- **portrayed(B)** is portray(B) by another name, the last of the two said
  standing.
- **A cycle's factors are S_1, S_2, ... under numbervars alone**, bound to
  `'$VAR'('S_N')` as swipl's writeTopTerm() binds them, so a portray goal
  is asked of one (`coco_write_cyclic`): write_term/2 with no numbervars,
  write_canonical/1, term_to_atom/2 and term_string/2 write the variables
  they are (`@(_A,[_A=f(_A)])`). Through 3.54.0 every write named them
  but write_term's variable_names(L), write_canonical/1's and the store's.
  The engine's own writes name them as before.
- **term_to_atom/2 and term_string/2 write swipl's PL_WRT_QUOTED alone**
  (mode 257): a string's quote doubled, `{}(a,b)` bare.
- **A failed portray goal's text takes no gap where a goal's text comes
  next** (`pgpg a`, where 3.54.0 wrote `pg pg a`): the machine's `wpgapb`
  and `wpgapq` name where the failed goal's text ended, a goal's text put
  there clears them, and an inner failed goal puts the outer's place back
  after its own (`pg g(pgzz+y)`).
- **An option's row is found once**: write_term/2's options are a table,
  `*wt-options*`, swipl's table with each option's kind, and one function
  made of it by a macro (`coco_wt_opt`: a cond on the name's first byte,
  then a strcmp a row of that byte's) serves the check and the write; the
  write takes the row in a switch. Through 3.54.0 the write compared each
  option with every name it applies, 13 strcmp an option, which the four
  names applied here would have made 17.

partial(B) is still checked and read past, where swipl starts the write
from the stream's last character (COMPAT.md); it is a task of its own.

cocolint's clause walker read a numeric escape's closing backslash before a
quote, `'\x2248\'`, as an escaped quote, and took test/files/write_escapes.pl
from its first quoted operator to its end for one clause of 11 914 bytes,
over the page budget (Z1). It reads the escape's digits and its backslash
whole now (`cc_escape_len` in tools/cocolint/clauses.pl); with the old
walker the new file lints with that one false Z1, with the new one clean.

test/files/write_escapes.pl, new, holds 240 lines to swipl, byte for byte;
3.54.0 differs at 144 of them. test/cyclic.pl's term_to_atom/2 of a cycle
expects swipl's variables, and its long and deep fixture's dotlists(true)
and no_lists(true) writes say numbervars(true), whose factors' names the
lengths it counts depend on. test/files/write_options.pl, 3.53.0's, is as
it was and green.

The arms, one build each, every rule taken out alone, each over
write_escapes.pl, write_options.pl, portray.pl, print.pl, write.pl and
test/cyclic.pl: the arm of no edit green in all six, and all nineteen
rules red in write_escapes.pl -- character_escapes(false), a string's quote

## write_term/2's partial(true), as swipl's (3.56.0)

partial(B) was the last of write_term/2's options checked and read past
(3.55.0's entry): every write began at no character, so `write(a),
write_term(b, [partial(true)])` wrote `ab` where swipl 9.0.4 writes `a b`.
swipl's pl-write.c begins a write after the last character written where
it goes, as PutOpenToken() asks the stream's lastc, which partial(false)
sets to none first: the write's first token takes a space where the two
would read as one -- `a b`, `1 2`, `- -a`, `+ -`. cocolog does the same
now, wherever the write goes. A minor, as what a program writes moves.

- **The write begins after PREV, the last character where it goes**:
  `coco_wt_put`'s new argument, put on the buffer before the term and taken
  off after it, the gap asked (`coco_write_gap_at`) where the portray mark
  is still the write's own -- what a portray goal wrote first owns its gap,
  as a goal's write is a write of its own in swipl. The partial write is a
  function of its own (`coco_wt_partial`) and the plain write a macro both
  use (`coco-wt-write`), so a write with no partial(true) pays the test of
  its option.
- **The console's user_output and user_error keep a last character each**
  (`coco_out_lc`, `coco_err_lc`), which `coco_out_note` notes from what the
  engine writes itself, where through 3.55.0 it kept only whether a line
  was open. A last byte past ASCII is decoded from its character's bytes
  (`coco_out_note_wide`, cold), a tail call at the note's end.
- **A capture keeps its own, from none at its start** (`coco_cap_lc`:
  with_output_to/2 and `~@`), and the outer capture's or the console's is
  put back at its end, in the word the start saved.
- **A file of library(stream) keeps its own** (`st_lc1`, 0 at the open),
  noted by `st_wrote` and `st_wrote_wide`, which every put and write passes:
  a byte a character in a stream of one byte a character (latin-1, octet,
  ascii), a code point decoded from the UTF-8 text in any other. Its
  write_term/3 writes into a capture, so `'$stream_lastc'/2` reads the
  stream's character before the capture begins -- user_output's and
  user_error's then still the console's (`coco_m_out_lastc`) -- and
  `'$stream_lastc_set'/1` hands it to the capture inside it.
- **format/3's `~W` begins after format's own text**, and at no character
  after a fill point (`~t`), where swipl's text is a sub-format's (-2,
  which turns partial(true) off); with nothing before it, after the
  sink's last character (`coco_fmt_lastc`: the console's, user_output's and
  user_error's, a stream of library(stream)'s through the module's hook,
  `coco_m_sink_lastc_install`, and a term sink none, as swipl begins each
  of those afresh).
- **A string's unquoted text clears the gap mark** a failed portray goal's
  text leaves (`pgs`, where 3.55.0 wrote `pg s`), as swipl's PutString
  makes no token check.
- **The journal runs `'$stream_lastc_set'/1`**: library(stream) is one of
  the modules whose every C predicate is a portal, which a replay answers
  from its line and does not run, and this one sets the engine's own state
  alone. Answered from the journal it left the capture at no character, so
  the text the next portal wrote was another, and the replay diverged
  there (`coco_jr_none`, the predicates of those modules that are none).
- **The SDK has three new calls** (lib/sdk.cicili, needing 3.56.0):
  `coco_m_sink_lastc_install`, `coco_m_out_lastc` and `coco_m_out_lastc_set`.

COMPAT.md's row for partial(true) is gone. Row 64, a write to user_output
by name inside a capture, which cocolog captures with the current output,
says what follows from it: a write_term/3 of user_output with partial(true)
there begins at the capture's last character, where swipl's begins at the
console's.

test/files/write_partial.pl, new, holds 151 lines to swipl, byte for byte
-- the console, stderr, captures nested and after, files in UTF-8,
ISO-Latin-1, UTF-16 both ways and binary, a slot reused, format's fill
points and stops, and portray goals' gaps -- and 3.55.0 differs at 77 of
them. test/journal.pl's new section records and replays a partial(true)
write to a stream: the stream's character journalled, the capture's set
not, and the replay ending where the record did.

The arms, one build each, every rule taken out alone, over
write_partial.pl, write_escapes.pl, portray.pl and write_options.pl. On the
first cut the arm of no edit is green in all four, and all 29 rules are red
in write_partial.pl alone: the option, the prefix, the gap's test and its

the notes of stdout, stderr and a capture, the capture's start and end, the

The journal's exemption taken out: test/journal.pl red at the new

The cost. The first cut counted 1.37 % more instructions on the

## halt/0,1 in a nested search ends the process, as swipl's (3.57.0)

swipl 9.0.4's halt/1 ends the process from whatever C called Prolog: a
findall/3's search, with_output_to/2's goal, a `~@' goal, a portray goal, a
cleanup a cut runs, a directive's search. cocolog's halt stopped the engine
it ran in and nothing more, so a nested search ended where it stood and the
program went on: `findall(X, (member(X, [1,2,3]), X >= 2, write(x(X)), nl,
halt(3)), L), write(L)' wrote `x(2)' and `[]' and exited 0, forall/2 went on
to the goal after it, and with_output_to/2's and `~@''s goal failed, exit 1.
Now the halt is the process's, with its code. A minor, as what a program
does moves.

- **A search hands its halt up** (`coco_halt_up' in lib/solve-loop.cicili):
  a sub engine stopped by halt/0,1 gives its `halted' and its code to the
  engine that started it, which stops at its next step, every engine out to
  the host's in turn. The builtin answers 2, having bound nothing -- the
  continuation stands, and the step loop's own test of `halted' does the
  rest, so the loop pays nothing.
- **findall/3 makes no answer of the search** (`coco_engine_findall', and so
  forall/2, aggregate_all/3, bagof/3 and setof/3): the trail and the heap
  wound back, the results dropped from the store.
- **call_limited/3 and call_metered/4 answer as for a ball caught** (3 to
  `coco_engine_call_limited''s callers), cocolog's own: swipl has neither.
- **A capture's goal that halts answers 5** (`coco_out_capture_run'):
  with_output_to/2 answers 2, its text dropped, as swipl's capture is never
  put out; `~@' ends the format there, kind 14, with what a failure leaves
  -- format's text before it put out, the goal's own where format holds no
  text for a column, nothing to a term sink; a portray goal stops the write
  (`wpstate' 5), its text and the write's before it kept, and the builtin
  answers 2 once they are out (print/1, write_term/2, `~p',
  print_message/2's line).
- **A cleanup that halts ends the cut that ran it** (`coco_engine_cut_slow'):
  no cleanup below it runs, as swipl's halt/1 runs none -- the host's cut of
  a goal that left a choice, with_output_to/2's, findall/3's search's.
  catch/3 takes no halt, as swipl's does not.
- **The toplevel's cut of an answer** runs a cleanup that may halt: the
  session ends with its code (cocolog.cicili's REPL, `quit').
- **A directive's search that halts ends the load and the process**: the
  load's goal hook already ended a load whose goal halted; a findall/3 in a
  directive's goal now halts that goal.
- **Under trace halt/0,1 has no Exit port**, as swipl's: the process ends at
  its Call. Through 3.56.0 the tracer printed `Exit: halt(28)`. The step's
  call of a builtin row and the `:' construct's print no Exit where the call
  set `halted' to 1; and a builtin whose search halted answers 2, so it has
  no Fail port either -- nothing failed.
- **'$trace_window'/4's run keeps its halt**: library(flow/debug) reports
  it as how the run ended, `halt(Code)', as it always has -- the one
  starter of a nested search that does not hand a halt up.

test/script.pl's three new sections. The first runs 22 programs, each a
child `run FILE "h(N)"' with its stderr in its stdout, and holds each text
and status to swipl 9.0.4's -- findall/3, forall/2, aggregate_all/3, nested
findall/3, catch/3 around one, setup_call_cleanup/3 around one, setof/3, a
cleanup a findall/3's search ran, with_output_to/2 and a findall/3 in it,
`~@' three ways and to a term sink, portray goals four ways and
print_message/2's, with_output_to/2's cut, the host's cut, two cleanups --
and 3.56.0 fails all 22. The second holds cocolog's own four:
call_limited/3, call_metered/4, the toplevel's cut and a directive's
findall/3 (3.56.0 fails those too, 26 in all). The third asks each of the 22
and the directive of the reference swipl 9.0.4 where there is one (`SWIPL'
may name it), so the wants are swipl's, and skips by name where there is
none. test/trace.pl's own lines hold the tracer's five: halt/1's Call
printed and no Exit for it; the system's halt/0 called as `system:halt'
over a program's own (`redefine_system_predicate(halt)', the `:'
construct's own call of the row), its Call printed and no Exit; and no Fail
port for with_output_to/2 whose goal halts. 3.56.0 prints both Exits, and
with_output_to/2's Fail and its clause's after it.

cocolint's card row H1 ("halt(N) inside a search ... ends only that
search") is retired: 24 rows, 34 cites, six patterns. Lesson 37 (its row
count and the row's history), the card's selftest, GUIDE.md, README.md and
library/main.pl's header follow; the token benchmark's card arm carries a

COMPAT.md had no row for a halt in a nested search; it has none now. Not
done (task 51, of its own): a name a program file took over that a
compiled-in module answers -- halt/1 after redefine_system_predicate/1,
msort/2 -- called through `system:' prints no port at all under trace,
where swipl prints its Call and Exit; the `:' construct traces an engine

The arms, one build each, every rule taken out alone, over test/script.pl
and test/trace.pl. The arm of no edit is green in both, three times over

## A load's source encodings, as swipl's (3.58.0)

swipl 9.0.4 reads a source file in an encoding: the one a BOM at its start
names, else the locale's; `:- encoding(E)' reads the rest of the file in E;
load_files/2's encoding(E) names it for the whole file; and an included file
is read in the encoding of the file that includes it. cocolog read every
file as UTF-8. A BOM's bytes were its first clause's, so the file began with
`illegal_character'. `:- encoding(utf8)' was an unknown procedure, reported.
A Latin-1 or UTF-16 file read as junk, and load_files/2 read past
encoding(E). Now each is swipl's. A minor, as what a program reads moves.

- **A BOM names the encoding and is taken off** (`coco_source_text' in
  lib/term.cicili): EF BB BF is UTF-8, FE FF UTF-16 big-endian and FF FE
  little-endian, swipl's ScanBOM() three. With none the file is UTF-8, where
  swipl's is the locale's (`text'). The function is the one reader of a
  source file: the hosts' `run FILE' and `consult FILE', a module's read,
  consult/1 and load_files/2, and an include.
- **The text a consult reads is UTF-8 whatever the file was**
  (`coco_text_cook'):
  - octet, ascii and iso_latin_1 are a byte a character;
  - UTF-16 is read either way round, a surrogate pair one character and a
    lone surrogate U+FFFD;
  - wchar_t is UCS-4 little-endian;
  - a NUL is C0 80, so the text stays a C string.
  A UTF-8 file with no NUL is read as it is, its BOM moved off; the cost is
  one memchr().
- **`:- encoding(E)' reads the rest of its file in E** (`coco_consult_owned'
  in lib/kb-consult.cicili, as swipl's '$source_term' sets the stream's
  encoding once the directive's term is read). The switch starts at the
  byte after its full stop (the reader's `fend'). The rest is written back
  in the class it was decoded from (`coco_text_raw') and decoded in E's
  (`coco_consult_recode'). The reader takes up the new text where it stood
  (`coco_reader_retext'), so every offset before it stands, a clause's place
  and a syntax error's alike. As in swipl, the full stop needs layout or a
  `%' after it in the encoding in force, so a switch to big-endian UTF-16
  cannot end its own directive.
  - `bom' changes nothing where it stands.
  - A name that is none ends the load with set_stream/2's error, as swipl's
    does: unbound, no atom, no encoding, or `'Utf-8''. The error is
    `instantiation_error', `type_error(atom, E)' or `domain_error(encoding,
    E)', in context system:set_stream/2; consult/1 raises it, and an `-s'
    script says `Prolog initialisation failed:' and exits 1.
  - A directive that `:- if(fail)' skips is no switch.
- **The names are swipl's** (`*coco-encodings*', one table, which a
  DEFMACRO makes into `coco_enc_class'): octet, ascii, iso_latin_1, text,
  utf8, unicode_be, unicode_le, utf16be, utf16le and wchar_t; the MIME names
  'UTF-8', 'ISO-8859-1', 'UTF-16BE' and 'UTF-16LE'; and bom. Case matters,
  as in swipl.
- **load_files/2's encoding(E) reads the file in E** (`lb_enc_option' in
  lib/library.cicili, swipl's '$set_encoding'):
  - The first encoding(_) of the options counts, whatever the BOM says.
  - `bom' takes the BOM's encoding, and a file with none reads nothing, as
    swipl's.
  - `default' reads nothing, as swipl's '$set_encoding' then fails.
  - It is checked as set_stream/2 checks it, once the file is found and is
    to be read: a missing file's existence error comes first, and an
    `if(not_loaded)' of a file loaded already checks nothing. Its errors are
    set_stream/2's.
- **An included file is read in the encoding of the file that includes it**
  (the include branch's `lenc'), as swipl's '$load_include' gives it the
  stream's encoding. Its BOM is taken off, and its own `:- encoding(E)'
  switches it.
- **A consult starts in the class its text was decoded from** (the machine's
  `lcls', taken at the consult's entry). That holds for the hosts' consults,
  consult/1's, a module read again, and a module's registered text, which
  keeps its class for every store's read of it (`cls' in lib/module.cicili).
  So a UTF-16 module's `:- encoding(utf16le)' changes nothing, and neither
  does a `:- encoding(iso_latin_1)' in a file loaded with that option.
- **A NUL byte is no end of the file.** Outside quotes it is
  `illegal_character', reported where it stands, and the load goes on, as in
  swipl. Inside a code list or a string it is the code 0, as it is after
  `0'': the lexer reads C0 80 as the NUL. In a comment it is nothing. A
  syntax error after it is placed as swipl places it, the NUL one column
  (`coco_raw_col_byte'). An atom ends at it, as an atom does at an escaped
  NUL (COMPAT.md). Through 3.57.0 the file ended at the NUL, unsaid.
- **Only a text that holds a NUL asks for one inside quotes.**
  `coco_text_cook' says whether it wrote one. The class's bit 16 carries
  that to the consult (`lcls'), and `coco_reader_init_nul' carries it to the
  reader (`nul'). An include's reader always asks, as its text is read
  after the consult began. The quoted loop is two copies of one DEFMACRO,
  `coco-lex-quoted-loop': the one a text with no NUL reads by asks nothing
  3.57.0's loop did not.
- **library(stream) takes the MIME names** (`stream_enc_id'), and
  stream_property/2 answers swipl's own name for an alias
  (`stream_enc_name'): utf16be for unicode_be, utf16le for unicode_le, utf8
  for 'UTF-8' and iso_latin_1 for 'ISO-8859-1'. The encodings of a stream
  itself have been swipl's since 3.19.0.

Five fields are appended: the machine gains `lenc' and `lcls', the reader
`fend' and `nul', and the module registry's entry `cls'. The SDK is
unchanged; `make modules' rebuilds library/stream.so.

test/files/encoding.pl is new: 186 lines held to swipl 9.0.4's, byte for
byte, and swipl's are the same in the C locale and under C.UTF-8. 3.57.0's
output misses 81 of them. The case writes every file it loads byte by byte,
and each file that holds a byte past ASCII names its encoding -- by a
directive, a BOM or the load's option -- because swipl's default is the
locale's. It prints codes. Its sections:

- the directive's names and refusals;
- switches within one file;
- the BOMs;
- the option;
- includes;
- modules;
- the NUL byte;
- library(stream)'s names.

Not compared, and in COMPAT.md: a byte that is no UTF-8, ascii's warning,
and `text' past ASCII.

The arms: one build each, every rule taken out alone, over the case. The arm
of no edit is green, on the first state and on the final one. Each of the 29

## `system:G' of a name a program file took over, as swipl's (3.58.1)

swipl's `system:G' reaches the system's predicate whatever user defines.
cocolog's `:' construct has called G's C row or module past a program
file's take-over since 3.1.0, but not all the way:

- A module row that turns some arguments down (`:declines') hands them to
  its Prolog half's clause, and the take-over had forgotten that clause.
  These are length/2 enumerating, last/2 of a partial list, reverse/2 with
  its first list unbound, nth0/3 and nth1/3 with the index unbound, and
  aggregate_all/3 of a template of templates. The declined goal was made
  `system:G' again and pushed, and ran for ever. So `system:length(L, N)'
  with length/2 redefined never answered, nor `system:last([a|_], X)' with
  last/2 defined, where swipl answers `[]-0' and `[a]-a'.
- Under trace, a module's answer had no port: `system:last([a, b, c], X)'
  printed nothing. Nor had a qualified goal nothing defines
  (`lists:nosuch').

A patch, as both were bugs and nothing new is reachable.

- **The library's own clauses of a taken name are kept** under
  `$system:NAME' of the same arity (`coco_kept_head' in
  lib/kb-consult.cicili):
  - by the take-over, where the library's half was read before it
    (`coco_pred_keep_muted');
  - by the assert, where it is read after: a module's half is read at a
    query's start, which comes after `run' consulted the program. Through
    3.58.0 the assert left such a clause out.
  A kept clause keeps the library's attributes, read at the take-over: 32,
  it hides its children, and 64, a library's. The program's clause decides
  the predicate's again after the take-over now, where it decided them
  before it, and before the fetch, which may refuse the clause. The first
  build copied them at the take-over and lost both, as the program's
  clause had cleared them.
- **A declined `system:G' runs them in the `:' step** (`coco_call_kept' in
  lib/solve-loop.cicili), as the step calls a predicate. Its frame's call is
  G's head under the kept name, so its clauses match it and their calls are
  hidden from the printer as a library predicate's are. A guarded frame's
  last call takes the guard on (`coco_det_pcall'). It is one step and one
  inference, as the row's answer is. Nothing kept is G's unknown procedure;
  every module the tree has that declines has its half's clause, so nothing
  reaches that.
- **What the tracer prints is G.** The tracer's context of a clause frame is
  the frame's call: a retry takes it, and the exit marker matches it. What
  it prints is its shadow frame's goal. These are one cell for every frame
  but the kept call's. So `system:length(L, N), N >= 1' prints length's
  Call, Exit, Redo and Exit as swipl's, and none of `'$skip_list'/3' and
  `'$length3'/3'. A kept frame that tries a clause before the one that
  answers -- aggregate_all/3's first clause tests its spec with var/1 --
  runs the next one's body as its own, hidden.
- **A guarded `system:G' answers alike whether its name is taken or not.**
  The kept call takes the guard on as the call of the name not taken does.
- **A qualified goal has the ports an unqualified one has**
  (`coco_colon_run'): the Call before anything runs, and a module's Exit and
  Fail too. A name nothing defines has its Call. The system's G hides its
  children; any other G is asked as the step asks it.

The kept predicate is named as the library's other `$' helpers are: a call
of `'$system:length'(L, N)' runs it, and predicate_property/2 of the head
named answers. Nothing that walks the program shows it: current_predicate/1,
predicate_property/2 with the head unbound, listing/0,1.

test/files/system_kept.pl holds 32 lines to swipl. Six of them are guarded
`system:G' goals of taken names, each answering as the name not taken does,
each predicate called once before, as swipl's first call of a library
predicate it autoloads keeps the guard on the caller (COMPAT.md).
test/trace.pl holds nine queries of test/trace-taken.pl to swipl's ports,
and two lines of its own. One is a qualified goal nothing defines, in a
clause that hides its children: swipl's catch/3 is a frame of its own, a
depth apart. The other is a kept frame's retry, the next clause's calls
hidden: swipl hides them too, but both show what aggregate_list/3's
maplist/4 calls, and swipl names its helper apply:maplist_/4.

What looked like two more differences is swipl's autoloader, COMPAT.md's
row of a library predicate's first call:

- swipl's first guarded call of a library predicate it has not loaded
  names the guarded clause (`gn/0', `dp/1'), where later ones name the
  callee (`lists:nth0/3', `lists:nth_gen/5');
- a guarded last call into a transparent library predicate that fails
  (maplist/2, aggregate_all/3 of a template of templates) raises on that
  first call alone.

Each later call answers as cocolog's, guarded `system:G' of a taken name
too. The first commit of these notes listed the two as not fixed.

Arms, one build each, 13. The arm of no edit is green. Eight rules are each
red in the files case or the trace case:

- the take-over keeping the library's clauses;
- the late read keeping them;
- the attributes read before the program's clause decides them (the arm
  read them after it);
- the kept call;
- a qualified goal's ports;
- the system's G hiding its children;
- the frame's call the kept head;
- the exit marker printing the goal.

Two were green, and each has a case now. The retry's context is held by the
trace case's line (without it the kept clause's three calls print). The
guard taken on by the kept call is held by system_kept's guarded lines
(without it `gq' raises and `gn' names its clause, where swipl and the
names not taken do neither).

Two were green and are gone:

- a traced cut matching the frame by its call: no clause a declined goal
  runs cuts;
- the clause as written renamed for the unifications moved into its head:
  the kept head's arguments are the head's own variables, so the move reads
  the same.

The cost. tools/flow/zero.sh against 3.58.0 at like paths, work less
padding: nrev 0, queens -3 636, lookup 0, of 40 to 66 million. The kept call
(`coco_call_kept') is out of line and cold, and the step loop's code is

## sub_atom/5 and sub_string/5 as swipl's sub_text() (3.58.2)

swipl's sub_atom/5 and sub_string/5 are one C function, sub_text() in
pl-prims.c, and what is given chooses its walk:

- two of Before, Length and After given are the third worked out: one
  answer and no choice point;
- one of them given walks the other two, its last answer leaving none;
- a bound Sub is a test where Before or After is given, and else a search
  that moves one place past each match and keeps its choice point only
  where the substring still fits there -- `ab' in `abcab' ends at 3 with
  none, `a' at 3 with one, which its redo fails;
- nothing given walks every Before and every Length.

cocolog's clauses walked Before and Length whatever was given, so:

- `sub_atom(A, B, 3, 0, S)' asked every place of A: 900 019 inferences and
  3.5 s on 100 000 characters;
- sub_string/5 cut a list of codes from the string's start at every place
  it tried (`'$sub_string'/5', length/2 and append/3 over string_codes/2):
  the search for a substring at the end of a string of 100 000 characters
  took 5 002 150 035 inferences and 254 s, and every suffix (After alone)
  was quadratic in either, 8 054 089 inferences and 1.8 s for 2 000
  characters;
- the walks' last answers left a choice point where swipl's leave none
  (`sub_atom(abc, B, 1, A, S)' at `c'), and a bound Sub's search left none
  at its last place where swipl's keeps one;
- `'$sub_atom'/6' asked an atom of a bound Sub, so `sub_atom(a12b, 1, L,
  A, 12)' failed, where swipl's PL_cmp_text() compares text.

Now sub_atom/5 and sub_string/5 are one clause each over the same seven
cases:

- `'$sub_text_length'/9' reads the arguments as sub_text() does, as /7 did
  (3.0.0), and hands back the text's length in bytes, which
  `'$atom_byte_length'/2' read again, and the case the given arguments
  make (`coco_bi_sub_text_length', the table in its comment);
- `'$sub_text_'/9' is a clause a case, its first argument the case, so no
  call asks what is bound: nothing given, Before, two of Before, Length
  and After, Length, After, a Sub alone or with Length, a Sub with Before
  or After;
- `'$sub_text'/8' cuts one substring where Before and Length say, a string
  for sub_string/5, with no walk from the start where a text's characters
  are its bytes, and works out whichever of Before, Length and After its
  clause leaves, Length from a Sub given. So the two cases that walk
  nothing are that call alone, and a walk binds only what it walks;
- a Sub given is a test, a memcmp and no term made, and whether it was
  given is the clause's word, `test', never what Sub is bound to when the
  C half runs: a walk binds Before or Length first, and a Sub that is the
  same variable is an integer then, which no substring unifies with.
  `sub_atom('1', 0, L, _, L)' fails in swipl. A first cut asked whether
  Sub was bound there and answered L = 1, and `sub_atom('01', _, B, _, B)'
  B = 1, both of which 3.58.1 had right;
- `'$sub_atom_positions'/6' finds a bound Sub's places in one scan, as /5
  did, gives the Sub's length (a Length given is compared), and ends the
  list `fits' where the last place leaves room, which `'$sub_search'/3'
  reads by its first argument's index.

`'$sub_atom'/6', `'$sub_string'/5', `'$sub_string_same'/2' and
`'$atom_byte_length'/2' are gone. A patch: swipl's answers and choice
points were cocolog's to match, and nothing new is reachable.

Not swipl's, and recorded in COMPAT.md: 9.0.4's search succeeds at the
last place the Sub fits whether or not its unifications did. Its
SUB_SEARCH goes to exit_succeed without asking `match', keeping what they
bound, so where Before, Length or After are one variable it answers what
no substring is: `sub_atom(abab, X, X, _, b)' X = 3 with After unbound,
`sub_atom(abab, X, _, X, b)' X = 3 with Length 1. cocolog answers what
the unifications give, none for either, as it copies no other bug of
swipl's.

test/files/sub_text.pl holds 1 210 lines to swipl. They cover every mode of
every answer of five texts, one past ASCII -- each of Before, Length, After
and Sub given or not, given as an answer gives it -- with whether each
answer left a choice point. Then come the failures and errors, a bound Sub
of another type, and arguments that are one variable (all but swipl's bug),
for both predicates. 3.58.1 gets 303 of them wrong. test/string.pl holds
the walks to what they cost: each mode with two of Before, Length and After
given costs the same on ten characters as on ten thousand, and Before and
Length given cost eight inferences.

Arms, one build each, 23. The arm of no edit is green. Twenty-one rules
are each red in the files case:

- a Sub given with Before, and one with After, a test;
- the search's `fits' end, and no `fits' where no place fits after;
- Length and After given, and Before and After, worked out;
- Length alone, After alone, Before alone and nothing given, each walking
  only to where the text ends;
- sub_string/5's string;
- a place in characters the bytes it covers;
- a Sub given compared as text;
- the length in bytes the length helper hands back;
- whether Sub was given the clause's word (the arm asks what Sub is bound
  to, the first cut's rule) and the test's clause saying so;
- a Length given beside a Sub given compared, in the test and in the
  search, and the search's Length the Sub's;
- three given adding up, and a place worked out below 0 failing.

Before and Length given walking nothing is green in the files case, a walk
of a Length given being a test, and red in string's: eight inferences
become ten. The check that each mode with two given costs the same on ten
characters as on ten thousand was vacuous as first written. st_cost/4 ran
once/1 on the mode itself, so the first call's answer bound the mode's
variables, and the second call, all given and wrong for the longer text,
failed out of the findall. The arms of Length and After and of Before and
After were green there. It takes the mode afresh now, and both are red there
too, as 3.58.1 is: 63 inferences against 89 973 for Length and After given,
and sub_string/5's 142 against 50 144 947.

The cost, by mode (inferences, 3.58.1 then 3.58.2; a short call ten
thousand times over `rep/2', which counts four of its own a call):

    100 000 characters, Length and After given        900 019       9
    100 000, Sub and After / Sub and Before                 16       9
    100 000, Before and Length given                        19       9
    100 000, Sub alone, first answer                        16      11
    100 000, Sub alone, every answer                   500 011 500 007
    100 000, Length alone, every answer              1 200 057 700 034
    2 000, After alone, every answer                 8 054 089  14 041
    100 000 string, Sub alone, first answer      5 002 150 035      11
    2 000 string, Length alone, every answer         2 057 103  14 036
    short, nothing given (x1 000)                      199 007 198 007
    short, Sub and After (x10 000)                     190 007 120 007
    short, Before and Length (x10 000)                 220 007 120 007
    short, Sub alone (x10 000)                         190 007 140 007
    short string, Sub alone (x10 000)                1 310 009 140 009
    short string, nothing given (x1 000)               541 009 198 009

In time, the walk of every Length on 100 000 characters goes from 3.5 s to
0.02, and the string's search from 254 s to nothing measurable.

Two cuts came first:

- The first kept the old shape's tests, an if-then-else over nonvar/1 in
  two clauses and `'$atom_byte_length'/2'. Every mode with Sub given cost 3
  to 6 inferences a call more than 3.58.1's, and its search 9 an answer
  where 3.58.1's was 5 -- a test of each place for the last one. The
  `fits' end and the case table took both back.
- The second had a clause for each of ten cases. Its walks bound the
  missing one of Before, Length and After in Prolog, and every start
  (`cocolog query true') read 107 220 instructions more than 3.58.1's,
  36.02 million against 35.91: ten clauses of nine arguments more to read,
  coco_next_token +29 000, strcmp +27 000, the parse +16 000, the store's
  put +15 000. It was also the cut that read a Sub bound at the C half as
  given.

With the C half working out what a clause leaves, the cases are seven, and
two of them are that call alone. Every mode costs what the ten-case cut's
did or less: a Sub with Before or After 9 where it was 12, a Sub alone 11
where it was 14, the After walk 14 041 where it was 16 045.

The start does 14 587 instructions less work than 3.58.1's, 35.90 million,
5 031 less with the padding set aside. tools/flow/zero.sh against 3.58.1 at
like paths, work less padding: nrev +102, queens -3, lookup -3 393, of 40
to 66 million.

Narrow cases green: lint, files, string, units, errors, library, engine,
trace, window, flowdebug, directives, script, reason, normalise and
translate, and the lessons that use sub_atom/5 or sub_string/5 (basics 08,
12 and 13; library 03, 13, 15, 17, 24, 26, 38, 46, 50, 51 and 55).
Reasoning stays 1.0.27.

## A write too deep for the C stack, and a cyclic term under a depth limit, as swipl's (3.59.0)

swipl's writeTopTerm() in pl-write.c does two things that cocolog did not.

First, with max_depth set, and cycles not false, it writes a term as it
stands, cyclic or not. The limit ends every path, so a cyclic term is the
tree it stands for, to the limit. cocolog's writer asked coco_acyclic of
the compound it met 1 024 levels down whatever the mode. So a cyclic term
under a limit past 1 024 was written in its factors:
`X = f(X), write_term(X, [max_depth(1500)])` was `@(_G1,[_G1=f(_G1)])`,
where swipl writes `f(f(...))` 1 500 deep (COMPAT.md had the row).

Second, it writes under C_STACK_OVERFLOW_GUARDED. A SIGSEGV on its
alternate signal stack jumps back, and the builtin raises
`error(resource_error(c_stack), context(system:write/1, _))`, its stream
keeping what the stack had room for. cocolog's writer recursed until the C
stack ran out: a tree some 43 000 levels of `f(...)` deep, or a deep limit
on a cyclic term, was a SIGSEGV, exit 139, in every write builtin.

Now:

- under a depth limit (mode 1024) no cycle guard asks, in the plain writer
  and in the one that asks the limit and portray (`coco_write_deep`,
  `coco_write_ask`);
- past 1 024 levels each compound asks `coco_cstack_room`, the calling
  thread's stack left above its floor. `coco_cstack_bounds` asks the system
  for the floor once a thread: glibc's pthread_getattr_np() and Darwin's
  pthread_get_stackaddr_np() and pthread_get_stacksize_np(). Neither is in
  Cicili's std, so they go through the raw-C escape, each declared where
  it is called. The floor is kept in two thread-local words. Before each
  portray goal the writer wants 256 KB of the stack, the goal running an
  engine of its own there;
- with under 64 KB left, the write stops as a cycle stops it
  (`coco_write_short_stop`: WSHORT, WCYC, and WDEEP 0, so every compound
  still to be written answers at once). The top of the write takes its
  text back and answers 0 (`coco_write_short_end`) once its factors' write
  has run short too: a tree that ran short runs short again in its
  factors, its stop the same. A listing's part does so at once, the guard
  put back for the clause's next part (`coco_write_pri`), and so do
  print/1's factors (`coco_write_portrayed`);
- each builtin raises `resource_error(c_stack)` with swipl's context once
  it has put out what came before: write/1, writeq/1, print/1,
  write_canonical/1, writeln/1, write_term/2,3, format/2,3 (`~w ~q ~p ~k
  ~W`, format's kind 15), term_to_atom/2 and term_string/2 (which bind
  nothing), portray_clause/1 and listing/1 (system:write_term/3, written
  over it in Prolog: `coco_cstack_error_wt`);
- a store refuses a clause it cannot write as a row: assertz/1 under
  `--embed` or a server raises `resource_error(c_stack)`, and a consult
  reports `Name/Arity: a clause too deep for the C stack to write` at the
  clause and reads on. The refusal leaves WSHORT set for no builtin to
  clear, so every write clears it as it begins, and so does a clause's
  layout for its parts;
- library(async) raises it where a goal or a term is too deep to hand over
  (go/2, channel_send/2, async_run/1) or a task's answer too deep to hand
  back (await/1, async_run/1);
- `statistics(c_stack, L)` is the thread's stack in bytes, and the
  uncaught error and print_message/2 say swipl's two lines:
  `C-stack limit (8,380,416 bytes) exceeded.` and `Use the shell command
  ulimit -s size to enlarge the limit.`

The writer stops at 42 983 levels of `f(...)` on 8 MB, 73 668 of
`[[...]]`, 4 749 of `f(...)` on 1 MB and 2 021 on 512 KB: some 190 bytes of
stack a level of `f(...)`.

Not swipl's (COMPAT.md):

- a write that ran out writes nothing to its stream, where swipl's stream
  keeps the 40 242 characters its stack had room for;
- statistics(c_stack) is the stack the system reports, 8 380 416 on the
  main thread (the rlimit less the pages above the stack's end), where
  swipl's is the rlimit, 8 388 608;
- in a thread but main swipl's message names thread_create/3's
  c_stack(KBytes) option, which cocolog's has not got (its threads have 8
  MB), and cocolog's names `ulimit -s` in every thread;
- library(thread)'s channel_send/2 and thread_create/2 of a term that deep
  raise `the term would not write`: its text is how a term crosses.

Found on the way, and the next two changes: the reader and is/2 recurse
too. `coco_parse_term` and `coco_parse_named` overflow at some 15 000
levels of `f(` or of a prefix operator, 16 500 of `[` and 20 000 of `(` or
of `,`, read from an atom on 8 MB. swipl's raises `resource_error(c_stack)`
for a bracket some 17 000 deep (from read_clause/3 in a load, which ends
there with the clauses before it kept) and reads a chain of 200 000
operators, prefix or `,`, its complex_term keeping a stack of its own.
coco_arith overflows at some 43 000 levels, where swipl's evaluates a
million.

test/files/cyclic_depth.pl holds 60 lines to swipl:

- fourteen cyclic terms under a limit past 1 024;
- seven deep trees, written and under a limit;
- two portray goals under a limit, and cycles(false) refusing;
- twenty writes that run out, each by its builtin with its context, two of
  them a cyclic term with a deep tree in it, whose factors' write runs out;
- six that hold that a write that ran out binds nothing and leaves the next
  write whole: term_to_atom/2's, write/1's, a deep limit's, a cyclic
  term's factors', portray_clause/1's and listing/1's.

It was the only files case to end in `:- initialization(main, main)`, which
the runner's `swipl -g main` ran a second time. It ends in none now.
test/cyclic.pl's new section holds what swipl does not end or has not got
(56 checks, above).

Arms, one build each, 34 (and L08's twice). The arm of no edit is green.
Thirty rules are each red in the files case, test/cyclic.pl's or both:

- under a limit, no cycle guard: in the plain writer and in the one that
  asks the limit and portray (files);
- past 1 024 levels the C stack asked (both), and 256 KB of it before a
  portray goal (cyclic: a goal that writes 500 levels of its own, under
  `ulimit -s 1024');
- the top's take-back once the factors' write ran short (cyclic: a cyclic
  term with a deep tree in it, on stdout), print/1's factors' (cyclic),
  and a listing part's, the guard put back (cyclic);
- each write clearing the flag as it begins (cyclic), and a clause's
  layout (cyclic);
- write/1 (both), writeln/1, write_canonical/1 and writeq/1 (files),
  print/1's and write_term/2's after their portray goals (both);
- format's ~W, ~w and ~q, and ~k (files), ~p and kind 15 (both);
- term_to_atom/2 and term_string/2 binding nothing, portray_clause/1 and
  listing/1 (files);
- assertz/1 under a store, and a consult's refusal of the clause (cyclic);
- statistics(c_stack), the uncaught error's two lines and
  print_message/2's (cyclic);
- library(async)'s: a task's answer too deep to hand back its error's
  text, a goal or a term too deep to hand over raising it, and none of its
  text taken (cyclic).

The listing part's take-back was green in both cases at first: the files
case runs short inside with_output_to/2, whose ball's text writes a term
and puts the guard back, and test/cyclic.pl's checks were the same. Without
it, a portray_clause/1 that ran short leaves the guard down, and the next

- a portray goal's call saving and restoring the flag of the write it is

  writes.
